```text
    (PrefixByLength.program true) PrefixByLength.Label.scan PrefixByLength.take 5 1
  intro z
  simpa using PrefixByLength.goes_total true z

/-- Dropping from the second component of a pair a prefix as long as its first
component is polynomial-time computable. Malformed inputs return `[]`.
**Proof sketch.** Use the same program in drop mode: skip the counted
prefix, then copy the remaining input. Its abstract time bound is still
`5(|z|+1)`, so compilation gives a polynomial-time machine. This is the
other splitting operation used in [AB09, §7.3, Theorem 7.8]. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_dropPrefixByLength :
    PolyTimeComputable PrefixByLength.drop := by
  apply CounterProg.polyTimeComputable_of_goes
    (PrefixByLength.program false) PrefixByLength.Label.scan PrefixByLength.drop 5 1
  intro z
  simpa using PrefixByLength.goes_total false z

end Complexity
```

```text
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePairing
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# One-pass transducers run in linear time

A *one-pass transducer* (a Mealy machine) reads its input once from left to right in a
finite control state, emitting at most one bit per input bit. This file realizes every
such transducer as a work-tape-free Turing machine running in time `|x| + 1`, so its
string function is polynomial-time computable. It is the machine-side tool behind
several reductions of [AB09, ch. 6]: the validator and output-clause stages of
`CKT-SAT ≤p 3SAT` ([AB09, Lem 6.11], `CircuitComplexity/CircuitSatReduction.lean`), the
marker stripping of the Karp–Lipton prefix language, and the field recoding of Meyer's
verifier.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.transduce` — the string function of a transducer with transition `δ` and
  emission `o`.
* `Complexity.transducerTM` — the machine running it.

## Main results

* `Complexity.transduce_nil`, `Complexity.transduce_cons` — the function's case lemmas;
  `Complexity.transduce_of_copy` — a state that copies and is kept gives the identity.
* `Complexity.transducerTM_computes` — the machine computes the transducer's function
  within `|x| + 1` steps.
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_transduce` — hence it is in FP.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the multi-tape machine; §6.1.2, Lemma 6.11.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

variable {σ : Type}

/-- The string function of a one-pass transducer: from control state `q`, each input
bit `b` emits `o q b` (one bit or nothing) and moves to `δ q b`. -/
def transduce (δ : σ → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) : σ → List Bool → List Bool
  | _, [] => []
  | q, b :: l => (o q b).toList ++ transduce δ o (δ q b) l

/-- A transducer emits nothing on the empty word: `transduce δ o q [] = []`. -/
theorem transduce_nil (δ : σ → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) (q : σ) :
    transduce δ o q [] = [] := rfl

/-- On `b :: l` a transducer emits `o q b` and continues from `δ q b`:
`transduce δ o q (b :: l) = (o q b).toList ++ transduce δ o (δ q b) l`. -/
theorem transduce_cons (δ : σ → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) (q : σ) (b : Bool)
    (l : List Bool) :
    transduce δ o q (b :: l) = (o q b).toList ++ transduce δ o (δ q b) l := rfl

/-- The transducer on a concatenation: run the first part, then the second part from the
state reached. -/
theorem transduce_append (δ : σ → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) (q : σ)
    (l₁ l₂ : List Bool) :
    transduce δ o q (l₁ ++ l₂) =
      transduce δ o q l₁ ++ transduce δ o (l₁.foldl δ q) l₂ := by
  induction l₁ generalizing q with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b l ih => simp [transduce, ih]

/-- **A copying state copies**: if from the state `q` every bit is emitted unchanged
(`o q b = some b`) and `q` is kept (`δ q b = q`), then the transducer started in `q` is the
identity, `transduce δ o q l = l`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `l`, by `Complexity.transduce_nil` and
`Complexity.transduce_cons`. -/
theorem transduce_of_copy (δ : σ → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) (q : σ)
    (hδ : ∀ b, δ q b = q) (ho : ∀ b, o q b = some b) (l : List Bool) :
    transduce δ o q l = l := by
  induction l with
  | nil => exact transduce_nil δ o q
  | cons b l ih =>
    rw [transduce_cons, hδ, ho, ih]
    rfl

/-- The transition table of the transducer machine: on a bit, emit, move right and change
state; on the right blank, halt. -/
def transducerTr (δ : σ → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) :
    σ → Option Bool → (Fin 0 → Option Bool) → Action 0 Bool σ
  | q, some b, _ => ⟨.pos, fun _ => (none, 0), o q b, some (δ q b)⟩
  | _, none, _ => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, none⟩

/-- **The transducer machine**: no work tapes, control states `σ`, started in `q₀`. -/
def transducerTM [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] (δ : σ → Bool → σ)
    (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) (q₀ : σ) : FinTM Bool where
  k := 0
  State := σ
  tm := { q₀ := q₀, tr := transducerTr δ o }

/-- The run of the transducer machine: from state `q` reading the suffix `x.drop i`, it
halts after `|x| - i + 1` steps having appended `transduce δ o q (x.drop i)`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the suffix: on a bit the machine emits `o q b` and steps
right (`inputSymbol_at` reads `x[i]`), on the right blank it halts. -/
theorem transducer_run [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] (δ : σ → Bool → σ)
    (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) (q₀ : σ) (x : List Bool) :
    ∀ (l : List Bool) (q : σ) (cfg : Cfg 0 Bool σ x) (i : ℕ), l = x.drop i → i ≤ x.length →
      cfg.state = some q → cfg.inputPos.val = i + 1 →
      ((transducerTM δ o q₀).tm.runFrom cfg (l.length + 1)).state = none ∧
      ((transducerTM δ o q₀).tm.runFrom cfg (l.length + 1)).output =
        cfg.output ++ transduce δ o q l := by
  intro l
  induction l with
  | nil =>
    intro q cfg i hl hi hq hp
    have hix : i = x.length := by
      have := congrArg List.length hl
      simp at this
      omega
    have hsym : cfg.inputSymbol = none := by
      rw [FinTM.inputSymbol_at cfg i hi hp]; simp [hix]
    simp only [List.length_nil, Nat.zero_add, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step,
      MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero]
    unfold MultiTapeTM.step
    rw [hq]
    simp only
    rw [hsym]
    simp [transducerTM, transducerTr, transduce]
  | cons b l ih =>
    intro q cfg i hl hi hq hp
    have hlt : i < x.length := by
      by_contra h
      rw [List.drop_eq_nil_of_le (by omega)] at hl
      exact List.cons_ne_nil _ _ hl
    have hb : x[i]? = some b := by
      have := congrArg List.head? hl
      simpa [List.head?_drop] using this.symm
    have hsym : cfg.inputSymbol = some b := by
      rw [FinTM.inputSymbol_at cfg i hi hp, hb]
    have hl' : l = x.drop (i + 1) := by
      have := congrArg List.tail hl
      simpa [List.tail_drop] using this
    rw [List.length_cons, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]
    have hstep : (transducerTM δ o q₀).tm.step cfg =
        ⟨some (δ q b), moveInputPos cfg.inputPos .pos, cfg.workTapes,
          fun i => cfg.workTapePos i + 0, cfg.output ++ (o q b).toList⟩ := by
      unfold MultiTapeTM.step
      rw [hq]
      simp only
      rw [hsym]
      simp only [transducerTM, transducerTr, Action.apply]
      congr 1
    have hp' : (moveInputPos cfg.inputPos .pos).val = i + 1 + 1 := by
      rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by omega)]
      simp [hp]
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := ih (δ q b) ((transducerTM δ o q₀).tm.step cfg) (i + 1) hl' (by omega)
      (by rw [hstep]) (by rw [hstep]; exact hp')
    refine ⟨h1, ?_⟩
    rw [h2, hstep]
    simp [transduce]

/-- **The transducer machine computes the transducer's function** within `|x| + 1` steps. -/
theorem transducerTM_computes [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] (δ : σ → Bool → σ)
    (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) (q₀ : σ) :
    (transducerTM δ o q₀).ComputesFunInTime (transduce δ o q₀) fun n => n + 1 := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := transducer_run δ o q₀ x x q₀ ((transducerTM δ o q₀).tm.initCfg x) 0
    (by simp) (by simp) rfl rfl
  exact (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ⟨h1, by rw [h2]; rfl⟩

/-- A one-pass transducer computes a polynomial-time function. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_transduce [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] (δ : σ → Bool → σ)
    (o : σ → Bool → Option Bool) (q₀ : σ) :
    PolyTimeComputable (transduce δ o q₀) :=
  polyTimeComputable_of_linear
    ⟨transducerTM δ o q₀, 1, fun x => by
      simpa only [Nat.one_mul] using transducerTM_computes δ o q₀ x⟩

end Complexity
```

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The TCSlib Authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Basic
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PClosure

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary comparison, addition and subtraction in polynomial time

Infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a result of the book. A pair of numbers is the
word `pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)`; every operation is defined on all words, reading
the components with `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal` (so malformed words count as `0`), and
outputs a normalized word `Nat.bits n` or a one-bit answer.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.BinArith.add`, `Complexity.BinArith.sub` — sum and truncated difference.
* `Complexity.BinArith.lt`, `Complexity.BinArith.le`, `Complexity.BinArith.beq` — comparisons.

## Main results

* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_add`, `polyTimeComputable_sub` — the carry and
  borrow chains are one finite-state scan (`Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_serial`)
  followed by normalization.
* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_lt`, `polyTimeComputable_le`,
  `polyTimeComputable_beq`, and the languages `lt_mem_P`, `le_mem_P`, `beq_mem_P`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§7.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace BinArith

open Turing LogProg

/-! ### Carry and borrow chains -/

/-- The carry out of a full adder with carry in `c` and bits `x`, `y`. -/
def carry (c x y : Bool) : Bool := (x && y) || (c && (x ^^ y))

/-- The sum (and difference) bit `x ⊕ y ⊕ c`. -/
def sumBit (c x y : Bool) : Bool := (x ^^ y) ^^ c

/-- The borrow out of a full subtractor computing `x - y - c`. -/
def borrow (c x y : Bool) : Bool := (!x && y) || (!(x ^^ y) && c)

/-- **The carry chain adds**: over `N` padded pairs of words of length at most `N`, the
output plus `2^N` times the final carry is `bitsVal a + bitsVal b + c`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `N`: a full-adder step satisfies `s + 2c' = x + y + c`, and
the scan of the tails accounts for the rest at weight `2`. -/
theorem serial_add : ∀ (N : ℕ) (a b : List Bool) (c : Bool), a.length ≤ N → b.length ≤ N →
    bitsVal (serialOut carry sumBit c (padZip a b N)) +
        2 ^ N * (serialState carry c (padZip a b N)).toNat =
      bitsVal a + bitsVal b + c.toNat := by
  intro N
  induction N with
  | zero =>
    intro a b c ha hb
    rw [List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : a.length = 0),
      List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : b.length = 0)]
    simp [padZip, serialOut, serialState, bitsVal]
  | succ N ih =>
    intro a b c ha hb
    have hbit : ∀ c x y : Bool,
        (sumBit c x y).toNat + 2 * (carry c x y).toNat = x.toNat + y.toNat + c.toNat := by
      decide
    have h := ih (a.drop 1) (b.drop 1) (carry c (a.headD false) (b.headD false))
      (by simp; omega) (by simp; omega)
    have h2 := hbit c (a.headD false) (b.headD false)
    rw [bitsVal_eq_headD a, bitsVal_eq_headD b]
    simp only [padZip, serialOut, serialState, bitsVal, pow_succ]
    linarith

/-- **The borrow chain subtracts**: over `N` padded pairs of words of length at most `N`, the
output plus `bitsVal b + c` is `bitsVal a` plus `2^N` times the final borrow.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `N`: a full-subtractor step satisfies `d + y + c = x + 2c'`. -/
theorem serial_sub : ∀ (N : ℕ) (a b : List Bool) (c : Bool), a.length ≤ N → b.length ≤ N →
    bitsVal (serialOut borrow sumBit c (padZip a b N)) + bitsVal b + c.toNat =
      bitsVal a + 2 ^ N * (serialState borrow c (padZip a b N)).toNat := by
  intro N
  induction N with
  | zero =>
    intro a b c ha hb
    rw [List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : a.length = 0),
      List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : b.length = 0)]
    cases c <;> simp [padZip, serialOut, serialState, bitsVal]
  | succ N ih =>
    intro a b c ha hb
    have hbit : ∀ c x y : Bool,
        (sumBit c x y).toNat + y.toNat + c.toNat = x.toNat + 2 * (borrow c x y).toNat := by
      decide
    have h := ih (a.drop 1) (b.drop 1) (borrow c (a.headD false) (b.headD false))
      (by simp; omega) (by simp; omega)
    have h2 := hbit c (a.headD false) (b.headD false)
    rw [bitsVal_eq_headD a, bitsVal_eq_headD b]
    simp only [padZip, serialOut, serialState, bitsVal, pow_succ]
    linarith

/-- Both component values of `z` are below `2^(|z|+2)`, the scan length used on `z`. -/
private theorem serial_bounds (z : List Bool) :
    bitsVal (pairFstD z) < 2 ^ (z.length + 2) ∧ bitsVal (pairSndD z) < 2 ^ (z.length + 2) := by
  have h1 := (bitsVal_lt_two_pow (pairFstD z)).trans_le
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) ((length_pairFstD_le z).trans (Nat.le_add_right _ 2)))
  have h2 := (bitsVal_lt_two_pow (pairSndD z)).trans_le
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) ((length_pairSndD_le z).trans (Nat.le_add_right _ 2)))
  exact ⟨h1, h2⟩

/-- On a word `z`, the final borrow of the subtraction scan decides `fst < snd`, and when it
is clear the scan's output is the difference. -/
theorem serial_sub_spec (z : List Bool) :
    serialState borrow false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)) =
        decide (bitsVal (pairFstD z) < bitsVal (pairSndD z)) ∧
      (bitsVal (pairSndD z) ≤ bitsVal (pairFstD z) →
        bitsVal (serialOut borrow sumBit false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)))
          = bitsVal (pairFstD z) - bitsVal (pairSndD z)) := by
  have h := serial_sub (z.length + 2) (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) false
    (by have := length_pairFstD_le z; omega) (by have := length_pairSndD_le z; omega)
  have hR := bitsVal_lt_two_pow
    (serialOut borrow sumBit false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)))
  rw [length_serialOut, length_padZip] at hR
  obtain ⟨ha, hb⟩ := serial_bounds z
  generalize 2 ^ (z.length + 2) = P at h hR ha hb
  cases hs : serialState borrow false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)) <;>
    simp only [hs, Bool.toNat_false, Bool.toNat_true] at h <;> simp at h ⊢ <;> omega

/-! ### Addition and subtraction -/

/-- The sum of the values of the two components of `z`, as a binary word. -/
def add (z : List Bool) : List Bool := Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z) + bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- The truncated difference `fst ∸ snd` of the values of the components of `z`. -/
def sub (z : List Bool) : List Bool := Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z) - bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- `add` on encoded numbers is addition. -/
@[simp] theorem add_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    add (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = Nat.bits (a + b) := by
  simp [add, bitsVal_bits]

/-- `sub` on encoded numbers is truncated subtraction. -/
@[simp] theorem sub_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    sub (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = Nat.bits (a - b) := by
  simp [sub, bitsVal_bits]

/-- **Binary addition is polynomial-time** (infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a
result of the book): the carry chain, then normalization.

**Proof sketch.** Scan `|z| + 2` padded pairs (`serial_add`); since `a + b < 2^{|z|+2}` the
final carry is `0`, so the output has value `a + b`, and `polyTimeComputable_normBits`
normalizes it. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_add : PolyTimeComputable add := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp (polyTimeComputable_serial carry sumBit false) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, add]
  congr 1
  have h := serial_add (z.length + 2) (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) false
    (by have := length_pairFstD_le z; omega) (by have := length_pairSndD_le z; omega)
  have hlt : bitsVal (pairFstD z) + bitsVal (pairSndD z) < 2 ^ (z.length + 2) := by
    have h1 := (bitsVal_lt_two_pow (pairFstD z)).trans_le
      (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (length_pairFstD_le z))
    have h2 := (bitsVal_lt_two_pow (pairSndD z)).trans_le
      (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (length_pairSndD_le z))
    have : 2 ^ (z.length + 2) = 4 * 2 ^ z.length := by ring
    omega
  generalize 2 ^ (z.length + 2) = P at h hlt
  cases hs : serialState carry false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)) <;>
    simp only [hs, Bool.toNat_false, Bool.toNat_true] at h <;> omega

/-! ### Comparisons -/

/-- The test `fst < snd` on the values of the components of `z`. -/
def lt (z : List Bool) : Bool := decide (bitsVal (pairFstD z) < bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- The test `fst ≤ snd` on the values of the components of `z`. -/
def le (z : List Bool) : Bool := decide (bitsVal (pairFstD z) ≤ bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- The test `fst = snd` on the values of the components of `z`. -/
def beq (z : List Bool) : Bool := decide (bitsVal (pairFstD z) = bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- `lt` on encoded numbers is `<`. -/
@[simp] theorem lt_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    lt (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = decide (a < b) := by simp [lt, bitsVal_bits]

/-- `le` on encoded numbers is `≤`. -/
@[simp] theorem le_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    le (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = decide (a ≤ b) := by simp [le, bitsVal_bits]

/-- `beq` on encoded numbers is `=`. -/
@[simp] theorem beq_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    beq (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = decide (a = b) := by simp [beq, bitsVal_bits]

/-- **Binary comparison `<` is polynomial-time**: the last bit of the scan emitting the
running borrow is the final borrow. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_lt : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [lt z]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_lastBit.comp (polyTimeComputable_serial borrow borrow false) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, lt]
  rw [getLastD_serialOut_self _ _ _ (by
    rw [← List.length_pos_iff, length_padZip]; omega), (serial_sub_spec z).1]

/-- **Binary comparison `≤` is polynomial-time** (`¬ snd < fst`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_le : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [le z]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_not (polyTimeComputable_lt.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSwap)
    using 1
  funext z
  by_cases h : bitsVal (pairSndD z) < bitsVal (pairFstD z) <;> simp [h, le, lt]
  omega

/-- **Binary equality is polynomial-time** (`≤` both ways). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_beq : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [beq z]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_and polyTimeComputable_le
    (polyTimeComputable_le.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSwap) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [le, beq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
    List.cons.injEq, and_true]
  by_cases h : bitsVal (pairFstD z) = bitsVal (pairSndD z)
  · simp [h]
  · rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne h with h' | h' <;> simp [h, h'.le, Nat.not_le_of_lt h']

/-- **Binary subtraction is polynomial-time**: `0` when `fst < snd`, else the borrow chain's
output, normalized. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_sub : PolyTimeComputable sub := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_ite polyTimeComputable_lt (polyTimeComputable_const [])
    (polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp (polyTimeComputable_serial borrow sumBit false)) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, sub, lt]
  by_cases h : bitsVal (pairFstD z) < bitsVal (pairSndD z)
  · simp [h, Nat.sub_eq_zero_of_le h.le, Nat.zero_bits]
  · simp only [h, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    rw [(serial_sub_spec z).2 (by omega)]

/-- The language `{⟨a, b⟩ : a < b}` is in `P` (components read by `bitsVal`; malformed words
read as 0). -/
theorem lt_mem_P : {z | lt z = true} ∈ P := mem_P_of_test polyTimeComputable_lt

/-- The language `{⟨a, b⟩ : a ≤ b}` is in `P` (components read by `bitsVal`; malformed words
read as 0). -/
theorem le_mem_P : {z | le z = true} ∈ P := mem_P_of_test polyTimeComputable_le

/-- The language `{⟨a, b⟩ : a = b}` is in `P` (components read by `bitsVal`; malformed words
read as 0). -/
theorem beq_mem_P : {z | beq z = true} ∈ P := mem_P_of_test polyTimeComputable_beq

end BinArith

end Complexity
```


## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassP/BinaryArith/Basic.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The TCSlib Authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Iterate
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Transducer
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Bin

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary words in polynomial time: normalization and bit-serial scans

Infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a result of the book. Numbers are the
little-endian words `Nat.bits n`, read back by `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal`, which accepts
every word (trailing zeros allowed). This file provides the word-level tools the arithmetic
of `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith` is assembled from.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.BinArith.padZip` — the bit pairs of two words, padded with zeros.
* `Complexity.BinArith.serialOut`, `Complexity.BinArith.serialState` — the output and the
  final state of a finite-state scan over bit pairs (a carry or borrow chain).

## Main results

* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_normBits` — `w ↦ Nat.bits (bitsVal w)`
  (dropping trailing zeros) is polynomial-time.
* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_lastBit` — the last bit of a word.
* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_serial` — a finite-state scan over the
  `|z| + 2` zero-padded bit pairs of the components of `z` is polynomial-time.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§7.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace BinArith

open Turing LogProg

/-! ### Values of words -/

/-- The value of a word is its head bit plus twice the value of its tail (any word). -/
theorem bitsVal_eq_headD (w : List Bool) :
    bitsVal w = (w.headD false).toNat + 2 * bitsVal (w.drop 1) := by
  cases w <;> simp [bitsVal]

/-- Appending a top bit `b` to `w` adds `b · 2^|w|`. -/
theorem bitsVal_append_singleton (w : List Bool) (b : Bool) :
    bitsVal (w ++ [b]) = bitsVal w + b.toNat * 2 ^ w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [bitsVal]
  | cons c w ih => simp only [List.cons_append, bitsVal, ih, List.length_cons, pow_succ]; ring

/-- A word has value `0` exactly when it has no `1`. -/
theorem bitsVal_eq_zero_iff (w : List Bool) : bitsVal w = 0 ↔ w.any id = false := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [bitsVal]
  | cons b w ih => cases b <;> simp [bitsVal, ih]

/-- The normalized word of a value fits in any word of that value: `|bits (bitsVal w)| ≤ |w|`. -/
theorem length_bits_bitsVal_le (w : List Bool) : (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length ≤ w.length :=
  length_bits_le (bitsVal_lt_two_pow w)

/-- If `n ≤ bitsVal w` and `|w| ≤ m`, then `Nat.bits n` has at most `m` letters. -/
theorem length_bits_le_of_le {n m : ℕ} (w : List Bool) (h : n ≤ bitsVal w) (hw : w.length ≤ m) :
    (Nat.bits n).length ≤ m :=
  (length_bits_mono h).trans ((length_bits_bitsVal_le w).trans hw)

/-! ### Small word maps -/

/-- Iterating `drop 1` drops a prefix. -/
theorem iterate_drop_one (w : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    (fun v : List Bool => v.drop 1)^[i] w = w.drop i := by
  induction i with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ i ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, List.drop_drop]

/-- The one-bit test "`w` contains a `1`" is polynomial-time (a one-state filter transducer
followed by the emptiness test). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_any : PolyTimeComputable (fun w : List Bool => [w.any id]) := by
  have ht := polyTimeComputable_transduce (σ := Unit) (fun _ _ => ())
    (fun _ b => if b then some true else none) ()
  have hnil : ∀ w : List Bool, (transduce (fun _ _ => ()) (fun _ b => if b then some true
      else none) () w = []) ↔ w.any id = false := by
    intro w
    induction w with
    | nil => simp [transduce]
    | cons b w ih => cases b <;> simp [transduce, ih]
  convert polyTimeComputable_not (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp ht) using 1
  funext w
  simp only [List.cons.injEq, and_true]
  cases h : w.any id <;> simp_all

/-- The chunk of the normalization loop: the head bit, if a `1` is still to come. -/
private def normChunk (w : List Bool) : List Bool := if w.any id then w.take 1 else []

/-- The normalization loop over all suffixes outputs the normalized word.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `w`: the first round emits the head bit exactly when a `1` is
still to come, and the remaining rounds output the normalized tail
(`Complexity.LogProg.bits_two_mul_add`). -/
private theorem flatMap_normChunk (w : List Bool) :
    ∀ N, w.length ≤ N →
      (List.range N).flatMap (fun i => normChunk (w.drop i)) = Nat.bits (bitsVal w) := by
  induction w with
  | nil =>
    intro N _
    simp [normChunk, bitsVal, Nat.zero_bits]
  | cons b w ih =>
    intro N hN
    obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ : ∃ M, N = M + 1 := ⟨N - 1, by simp at hN; omega⟩
    rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_map]
    simp only [List.drop_zero, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, List.drop_succ_cons]
    rw [ih N (by simpa using hN)]
    cases hb : (b :: w).any id
    · have h0 : bitsVal (b :: w) = 0 := (bitsVal_eq_zero_iff _).mpr hb
      have hw : bitsVal w = 0 := by simp only [bitsVal] at h0; omega
      simp [normChunk, hb, h0, hw, Nat.zero_bits]
    · have hb' : bitsVal w = 0 → b = true := by
        intro h0
        have := (bitsVal_eq_zero_iff w).mp h0
        simpa [this] using hb
      simp only [normChunk, hb, if_true, List.take_succ_cons, List.take_zero, List.singleton_append]
      rw [show bitsVal (b :: w) = 2 * bitsVal w + b.toNat by simp [bitsVal]; ring,
        bits_two_mul_add _ _ hb']

/-- **Normalization is polynomial-time**: `w ↦ Nat.bits (bitsVal w)` (drop the trailing
zeros) is polynomial-time, by the emit loop over the suffixes of `w`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_normBits :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun w => Nat.bits (bitsVal w)) := by
  have he : PolyTimeComputable normChunk :=
    polyTimeComputable_ite polyTimeComputable_any polyTimeComputable_take1
      (polyTimeComputable_const [])
  have h := polyTimeComputable_emitIter polyTimeComputable_tail he 1 1 1 1 (fun w i => by
    rw [iterate_drop_one, List.length_drop]; simp; omega)
  convert h using 1
  funext w
  simp only [iterate_drop_one]
  exact (flatMap_normChunk w _ (by simp; omega)).symm

/-- The chunk of the last-bit loop: the head bit of a one-letter suffix. -/
private def lastChunk (w : List Bool) : List Bool := if w.drop 1 = [] then w.take 1 else []

/-- The last-bit loop over all suffixes outputs the last bit, if any. -/
private theorem flatMap_lastChunk (w : List Bool) :
    ∀ N, w.length ≤ N →
      (List.range N).flatMap (fun i => lastChunk (w.drop i)) = w.getLast?.toList := by
  induction w with
  | nil => intro N _; simp [lastChunk]
  | cons b w ih =>
    intro N hN
    obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ : ∃ M, N = M + 1 := ⟨N - 1, by simp at hN; omega⟩
    rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_map]
    simp only [List.drop_zero, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, List.drop_succ_cons]
    rw [ih N (by simpa using hN)]
    cases w with
    | nil => simp [lastChunk]
    | cons c w => simp [lastChunk]

/-- **The last bit is polynomial-time**: `w ↦ [w.getLastD false]`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_lastBit :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun w : List Bool => [w.getLastD false]) := by
  have hnil : PolyTimeComputable (fun w : List Bool => [decide (w.drop 1 = [])]) :=
    polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp polyTimeComputable_tail
  have he : PolyTimeComputable lastChunk := by
    convert polyTimeComputable_ite hnil polyTimeComputable_take1 (polyTimeComputable_const [])
      using 1
    funext w
    simp [lastChunk]
  have h := polyTimeComputable_emitIter polyTimeComputable_tail he 1 1 1 1 (fun w i => by
    rw [iterate_drop_one, List.length_drop]; simp; omega)
  convert polyTimeComputable_headD.comp h using 1
  funext w
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, iterate_drop_one]
  rw [flatMap_lastChunk w _ (by simp; omega)]
  rcases h : w.getLast? with _ | v <;> simp [h]

/-! ### Slots, bits and Boolean helpers -/

/-- The second slot `B` of a state `⟨A, ⟨B, C⟩⟩` is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_slot2 : PolyTimeComputable (fun S => pairFstD (pairSndD S)) :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD

/-- The third slot `C` of a state `⟨A, ⟨B, C⟩⟩` is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_slot3 : PolyTimeComputable (fun S => pairSndD (pairSndD S)) :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD

/-- Prepending a computed bit to a computed word is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_cons {p : List Bool → Bool} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hp : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [p x])) (hf : PolyTimeComputable f) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun x => p x :: f x) :=
  hp.append hf

/-- The fourth slot `q` of a state `⟨b, ⟨R, ⟨r, q⟩⟩⟩` is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_slot4 :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun S => pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD S))) :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_slot3

/-- Exclusive or of two one-bit tests is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_xor {p q : List Bool → Bool}
    (hp : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [p x])) (hq : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [q x])) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [p x ^^ q x]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_ite hp (polyTimeComputable_not hq) hq using 1
  funext x
  cases p x <;> simp

/-- Dropping a fixed number of leading bits is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_drop (i : ℕ) : PolyTimeComputable (fun w : List Bool => w.drop i) := by
  induction i with
  | zero => exact polyTimeComputable_id
  | succ i ih =>
    convert polyTimeComputable_tail.comp ih using 1
    funext w
    simp

/-- Dropping the low bit halves the value. -/
theorem bitsVal_drop_one (w : List Bool) : bitsVal (w.drop 1) = bitsVal w / 2 := by
  have := bitsVal_eq_headD w; have := Bool.toNat_le (w.headD false); omega

/-- The parity of a word's value is its low bit. -/
theorem bitsVal_mod_two (w : List Bool) : bitsVal w % 2 = (w.headD false).toNat := by
  have := bitsVal_eq_headD w; have := Bool.toNat_le (w.headD false); omega

/-! ### Bit pairs and finite-state scans -/

/-- The first `N` bit pairs of `a` and `b`, each padded with zeros. -/
def padZip : List Bool → List Bool → ℕ → List (Bool × Bool)
  | _, _, 0 => []
  | a, b, N + 1 => (a.headD false, b.headD false) :: padZip (a.drop 1) (b.drop 1) N

/-- `padZip a b N` has `N` pairs. -/
@[simp] theorem length_padZip (a b : List Bool) (N : ℕ) : (padZip a b N).length = N := by
  induction N generalizing a b with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ N ih => simp [padZip, ih]

/-- The output of a finite-state scan over bit pairs: in state `s`, the pair `(x, y)` emits
`o s x y` and moves to `δ s x y`. -/
def serialOut {σ : Type} (δ : σ → Bool → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Bool → Bool) :
    σ → List (Bool × Bool) → List Bool
  | _, [] => []
  | s, p :: ps => o s p.1 p.2 :: serialOut δ o (δ s p.1 p.2) ps

/-- The final state of a finite-state scan over bit pairs. -/
def serialState {σ : Type} (δ : σ → Bool → Bool → σ) : σ → List (Bool × Bool) → σ
  | s, [] => s
  | s, p :: ps => serialState δ (δ s p.1 p.2) ps

/-- A scan emits one bit per pair. -/
@[simp] theorem length_serialOut {σ : Type} (δ : σ → Bool → Bool → σ)
    (o : σ → Bool → Bool → Bool) (s : σ) (ps : List (Bool × Bool)) :
    (serialOut δ o s ps).length = ps.length := by
  induction ps generalizing s with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons p ps ih => simp [serialOut, ih]

/-- When a scan emits its new state, its last output bit is its final state. -/
theorem getLastD_serialOut_self (δ : Bool → Bool → Bool → Bool) (s : Bool)
    (ps : List (Bool × Bool)) (hps : ps ≠ []) :
    (serialOut δ δ s ps).getLastD false = serialState δ s ps := by
  induction ps generalizing s with
  | nil => exact absurd rfl hps
  | cons p ps ih =>
    cases ps with
    | nil => simp [serialOut, serialState]
    | cons q qs =>
      have := ih (δ s p.1 p.2) (List.cons_ne_nil _ _)
      simp only [serialOut, serialState] at this ⊢
      simpa using this

/-- The transition of the bit-level transducer running a scan over pairs: the first bit of a
pair is buffered, the second one fires the scan's transition. -/
def pairδ {σ : Type} (δ : σ → Bool → Bool → σ) : Option Bool × σ → Bool → Option Bool × σ
  | (none, s), x => (some x, s)
  | (some x, s), y => (none, δ s x y)

/-- The emission of the bit-level transducer running a scan over pairs. -/
def pairO {σ : Type} (o : σ → Bool → Bool → Bool) : Option Bool × σ → Bool → Option Bool
  | (none, _), _ => none
  | (some x, s), y => some (o s x y)

/-- The bit-level transducer on the flattened pairs is the scan. -/
theorem transduce_pairs {σ : Type} (δ : σ → Bool → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Bool → Bool)
    (s : σ) (ps : List (Bool × Bool)) :
    transduce (pairδ δ) (pairO o) (none, s) (ps.flatMap fun p => [p.1, p.2]) =
      serialOut δ o s ps := by
  induction ps generalizing s with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons p ps ih => simp [transduce, pairδ, pairO, serialOut, ih]

/-- The emitted pairs of the zip loop over `N` rounds are the flattened padded pairs. -/
private theorem flatMap_zipChunk (a b : List Bool) (N : ℕ) :
    (List.range N).flatMap (fun i => [(a.drop i).headD false, (b.drop i).headD false]) =
      (padZip a b N).flatMap (fun p => [p.1, p.2]) := by
  induction N generalizing a b with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ N ih =>
    rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_map, padZip, List.flatMap_cons]
    simp only [List.drop_zero, Nat.succ_eq_add_one]
    rw [← ih (a.drop 1) (b.drop 1)]
    simp

/-- The round of the zip loop: drop the head of both components. -/
private def zipStep (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode ((pairFstD w).drop 1) ((pairSndD w).drop 1)

/-- The iterates of the zip loop: after `i + 1` rounds both components lost `i + 1` bits. -/
private theorem iterate_zipStep (w : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    zipStep^[i + 1] w = pairEncode ((pairFstD w).drop (i + 1)) ((pairSndD w).drop (i + 1)) := by
  induction i with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ i ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih]
    simp [zipStep]

/-- The flattened zero-padded bit pairs of the two components of `z`, `|z| + 2` pairs long,
are polynomial-time (an emit loop dropping one bit of each component per round).

**Proof sketch.** After `i` rounds the state is `⟨a.drop i, b.drop i⟩`, never longer than
`|z| + 2`, and round `i` emits the two `i`-th bits (`flatMap_zipChunk`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_zipStream :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z => (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)).flatMap
      (fun p => [p.1, p.2])) := by
  have hg : PolyTimeComputable zipStep :=
    (polyTimeComputable_tail.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_tail.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have he : PolyTimeComputable
      (fun w => [(pairFstD w).headD false] ++ [(pairSndD w).headD false]) :=
    (polyTimeComputable_headD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).append
      (polyTimeComputable_headD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have h := polyTimeComputable_emitIter hg he 1 1 2 1 (fun w i => by
    cases i with
    | zero => simp; omega
    | succ i =>
      rw [iterate_zipStep, length_pairEncode, List.length_drop, List.length_drop]
      have := length_pair_components_le w
      simp; omega)
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  rw [← flatMap_zipChunk]
  simp only [one_mul, pow_one, Nat.add_assoc, Nat.reduceAdd]
  refine List.flatMap_congr (fun i _ => ?_)
  cases i with
  | zero => simp
  | succ i => rw [iterate_zipStep]; simp

/-- **Finite-state scans are polynomial-time**: the scan `(δ, o)` from state `s` over the
`|z| + 2` zero-padded bit pairs of the components of `z` (the transducer `pairδ`/`pairO`
after the zip loop). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_serial {σ : Type} [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]
    (δ : σ → Bool → Bool → σ) (o : σ → Bool → Bool → Bool) (s : σ) :
    PolyTimeComputable
      (fun z => serialOut δ o s (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2))) := by
  convert (polyTimeComputable_transduce (pairδ δ) (pairO o) (none, s)).comp
    polyTimeComputable_zipStream using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, transduce_pairs]

end BinArith

end Complexity
```

```text
/-
```
