```text
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Experiments
import TCSlib.Cryptography.OneWayFunctions.Basic
import TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Size

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Sampling devices: statistical closeness, rejection sampling, random permutations

The one sampling device of the Pass–shelat campaign (foundation decision D10). Experiments
are stated with *ideal* uniform distributions, exactly as in [PS10]; honest parties and
reductions, which only have uniform coin strings, sample these distributions by truncated
rejection sampling, and every theorem carries the explicit statistical term. The file is
concrete-layer only: no machines, one security parameter at a time.

* `StatClose X Y δ` — two samplers from uniform seeds are statistically `δ`-close: every
  test set has probabilities under the two laws differing by at most `δ` (the
  sup-over-test-sets form of the statistical distance, usable for samples in an infinite type
  such as `List Bool`). It is closed under post-processing (`StatClose.map`), products
  (`StatClose.prod`), composition (`StatClose.trans`) and reparametrisation of the seed by a
  uniform-preserving map (`StatClose.comp_pushesUniform`), and bounds every distinguishing
  advantage (`distAdv_le_of_statClose`) and, more generally, every success probability of an
  experiment with auxiliary coins (`StatClose.abs_uprob_sub_le_prod`) — the statistical-switch
  lemma C10 of the Chapter 2 inventory.
* `HardcoreBit.PushesUniform` from equal fibres (`pushesUniform_of_card_fiber`, lemma C5): a map
  all of whose fibres have the same size pushes uniform to uniform (`QR_N` sampling by squaring,
  [PS10, Corollary 60.6, Theorem 63.10]).
* `firstHit E xs` — the first of `T` draws satisfying `E`: uniform on `E` conditioned on
  existence, and no hit with probability `(1 - Pr[E])^T` (lemma C4, [PS10, Lemma 51.17]).
* `rejectionSample m k T` — `T` trials of `k` bits read as a number, the first one below `m`:
  uniform on `Fin m` conditioned on `some`, `none` with probability `(1 - m/2^k)^T`, and the
  total sampler obtained by falling back to a default is `StatClose` to uniform within that
  term. This is the uniform position of [PS10, Theorem 35.1] and the samplers of `Π_n`, `Z_q`,
  `Z_N^*` and `QR_N` of [PS10, §2.6–§2.12].
* `statClose_getD_of_uniform_of_some` — a sampler that is uniform conditioned on success,
  made total by a default, is `StatClose` to uniform within its failure probability (C4 in
  abstract form); `one_sub_inv_pow_le_half` — `(1 - 1/m)^m ≤ 1/2`, the dyadic form of
  "`(1 - 1/m)^m ≈ e^{-1}`" used for the closed forms of the failure terms.
* The permutation sampler `permFromCoins n k T` (Fisher–Yates with rejection-sampled
  offsets, the permutations of [PS10, Protocols 118.3, 120.6 and 127.5]) and the campaign
  parameters `permBits`, `permTrials` live in `Asymptotic/Permutations.lean`
  (file-size limit).

**Deviation:** [PS10] samples primes, residues and permutations exactly, in expected
polynomial time; here every such sampler is truncated to `T` trials and the experiments carry
an explicit statistical term (D10, deviations register #15).

**Repair (run-3 audit P2-1):** the general closeness lemma `statClose_getD_of_uniform_of_some`,
the seed reparametrisation `StatClose.comp_pushesUniform` and `one_sub_inv_pow_le_half` were
added for the permutation sampler, whose section moved to `Asymptotic/Permutations.lean`.

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.StatClose` — statistical `δ`-closeness of two samplers.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.bitsToNat`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.bitsEquiv` — a `k`-bit string as a
  number below `2^k`, and the resulting bijection with `Fin (2^k)`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.uniformFromBits`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.rejectionSample` — one rejection
  trial, and `T` trials.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.firstHit` — the first of `T` draws satisfying a predicate.

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.StatClose.abs_uprob_sub_le_prod`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.distAdv_le_of_statClose` — the statistical-switch lemma (C10).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.StatClose.map`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.StatClose.prod`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.StatClose.trans`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.StatClose.comp_pushesUniform`
  — closure properties.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.pushesUniform_of_card_fiber` — equal fibres push uniform to uniform (C5).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.firstHit_uniform_of_some`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.uprob_firstHit_none`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.statClose_firstHit` — the first hit is uniform (C4).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.rejectionSample_uniform_of_some`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.uprob_rejectionSample_none`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.statClose_rejectionSample` — the rejection sampler.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.statClose_getD_of_uniform_of_some` — a sampler that is uniform
  conditioned on success, made total by a default, is close to uniform within its failure
  probability (C4 in abstract form).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.one_sub_inv_pow_le_half` — `(1 - 1/m)^m ≤ 1/2`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.statClose_one`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.abs_uexp_sub_le`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.foldl_bits_eq`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.two_pow_size_le_two_mul` — glue:
  any two samplers are `1`-close, averages of pointwise close functions are close, the binary
  fold with an accumulator, and `2^{size m} ≤ 2m`.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (Definition 181.1, `ε`-closeness; §2.4.2 Theorem 35.1; §2.6.5 Lemma 51.17; §2.12
  Corollary 60.6 and Theorem 63.10; §4.4–§4.6 Protocols 120.6 and 127.5 for the permutation
  sampler of `Asymptotic/Permutations.lean`.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, Lemma 3.1 (statistical distance bounds every advantage).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Finset

/-! ### Statistical closeness -/

/-- Two samplers `X : σ → γ` and `Y : τ → γ` from uniform seeds are *statistically
`δ`-close* when every test set `T ⊆ γ` has probabilities under the two sampled laws differing
by at most `δ`: the `ε`-closeness of [PS10, Definition 181.1] ("for every (deterministic)
distinguisher `D` (with no time bound), `|Pr[D(x) = 1] − Pr[D(y) = 1]| ≤ ε`"), in its
sup-over-test-sets form, usable for samples in an infinite type such as `List Bool`; on a
finite sample space, with nonempty seed types, it is exactly `EpsClose` of the two laws
(`statClose_iff_epsClose_map`, `Asymptotic/SamplingFinDist.lean`). The device of foundation
decision D10: experiments use ideal distributions, samplers approximate them within
`StatClose` error [PS10, §2.4.2 (the uniform position of Theorem 35.1), §4.3 (statistical
zero-knowledge)].

The seed types are not required to be nonempty. On an empty seed type every probability is
`0` (`uprob`), so the "law" of an empty-seeded sampler is the zero measure and
`StatClose X Y 0` fails as soon as `Y` has seeds; every use has nonempty seeds
(`Ensemble.nonempty`, machine coins `Fin k → Bool`, the `[Nonempty σ]` of `SamplingFinDist`). -/
def StatClose {σ τ γ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ T : γ → Prop, |uprob (fun s => T (X s)) - uprob (fun t => T (Y t))| ≤ δ

section StatClose

variable {σ τ υ γ γ' : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ] [Fintype υ]

/-- The defining property of `StatClose`: `StatClose X Y δ` iff
`|Pr_s[T (X s)] − Pr_t[T (Y t)]| ≤ δ` for every test set `T`. -/
theorem statClose_iff (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (δ : ℝ) :
    StatClose X Y δ ↔ ∀ T : γ → Prop, |uprob (fun s => T (X s)) - uprob (fun t => T (Y t))| ≤ δ :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- Unfolding: for a `δ`-close pair the probability of any test set moves by at most `δ`. -/
theorem StatClose.abs_uprob_sub_le {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ} (h : StatClose X Y δ)
    (T : γ → Prop) : |uprob (fun s => T (X s)) - uprob (fun t => T (Y t))| ≤ δ :=
  h T

/-- One-sided form: the probability of a test set under `X` is at most its probability under
`Y` plus `δ`. -/
theorem StatClose.uprob_le_add {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ} (h : StatClose X Y δ)
    (T : γ → Prop) : uprob (fun s => T (X s)) ≤ uprob (fun t => T (Y t)) + δ := by
  linarith [(abs_le.1 (h T)).2]

/-- A closeness bound is nonnegative. -/
theorem StatClose.nonneg {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ} (h : StatClose X Y δ) : 0 ≤ δ :=
  (abs_nonneg _).trans (h fun _ => True)

/-- A sampler is `0`-close to itself. -/
theorem StatClose.refl (X : σ → γ) : StatClose X X 0 := fun _ => by
  rw [sub_self, abs_zero]

/-- Closeness is symmetric. -/
theorem StatClose.symm {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ} (h : StatClose X Y δ) :
    StatClose Y X δ := fun T => by
  rw [abs_sub_comm]
  exact h T

/-- A closeness bound may be weakened. -/
theorem StatClose.mono {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ δ' : ℝ} (h : StatClose X Y δ) (hδ : δ ≤ δ') :
    StatClose X Y δ' := fun T => (h T).trans hδ

/-- Closeness bounds add along a chain (triangle inequality). -/
theorem StatClose.trans {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {Z : υ → γ} {δ δ' : ℝ}
    (h : StatClose X Y δ) (h' : StatClose Y Z δ') : StatClose X Z (δ + δ') := fun T =>
  (abs_sub_le _ _ _).trans (add_le_add (h T) (h' T))

/-- Post-processing both samplers by the same function preserves closeness: the test set `T`
for the images is the test set `T ∘ g` for the sources (statistical-switch lemma C10,
first half). -/
theorem StatClose.map {σ τ γ γ' : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ] {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ}
    (h : StatClose X Y δ) (g : γ → γ') : StatClose (fun s => g (X s)) (fun t => g (Y t)) δ :=
  fun T => h fun c => T (g c)

/-- Relabelling the seed space of the first sampler by a bijection preserves closeness. -/
theorem StatClose.comp_equiv_left {σ' : Type*} [Fintype σ'] {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ}
    (h : StatClose X Y δ) (e : σ' ≃ σ) : StatClose (fun s => X (e s)) Y δ := fun T => by
  rw [uprob_comp_equiv e (fun s => T (X s))]
  exact h T

/-- Relabelling the seed space of the second sampler by a bijection preserves closeness. -/
theorem StatClose.comp_equiv_right {τ' : Type*} [Fintype τ'] {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ}
    (h : StatClose X Y δ) (e : τ' ≃ τ) : StatClose X (fun t => Y (e t)) δ := fun T => by
  rw [uprob_comp_equiv e (fun t => T (Y t))]
  exact h T

/-- A map pushing uniform to uniform is `0`-close to the identity sampler: an exact sampler
(for example squaring onto `QR_N`, lemma C5) has no statistical term. -/
theorem statClose_of_pushesUniform {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Fintype γ] {π : Ω → γ}
    (h : HardcoreBit.PushesUniform π) : StatClose π (id : γ → γ) 0 := fun T => by
  rw [h.uprob_eq T]
  simp

/-- Precomposing the first sampler with a map that pushes uniform to uniform (for example
reading a party's random tape as a coin table, `pushesUniform_coinTable`) preserves
closeness: the law of `X ∘ π` is the law of `X`.

**Repair (run-3 audit P2-1):** added for the string-level permutation samplers. -/
theorem StatClose.comp_pushesUniform {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ}
    (h : StatClose X Y δ) {π : Ω → σ} (hπ : HardcoreBit.PushesUniform π) :
    StatClose (fun ω => X (π ω)) Y δ := fun T => by
  rw [hπ.uprob_eq (fun s => T (X s))]
  exact h T

/-- **Averages of pointwise `c`-close functions are `c`-close**: for `0 ≤ c` and
`|f a − g a| ≤ c` for all `a`, `|uexp f − uexp g| ≤ c` (`0 ≤ c` covers the empty type). -/
theorem abs_uexp_sub_le {α : Type*} [Fintype α] {f g : α → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c)
    (h : ∀ a, |f a - g a| ≤ c) : |uexp f - uexp g| ≤ c := by
  rw [← HardcoreBit.uexp_sub, uexp_def]
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (Fintype.card α) with h0 | hpos
  · rw [h0]
    simpa using hc
  · have hc' : (0 : ℝ) < Fintype.card α := by exact_mod_cast hpos
    rw [abs_div, abs_of_pos hc', div_le_iff₀ hc']
    calc |∑ a, (f a - g a)| ≤ ∑ a, |f a - g a| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ _a : α, c := Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => h a
      _ = c * Fintype.card α := by rw [sum_const, card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm]

/-- **Any two samplers are `1`-close**: `StatClose X Y 1`, since both probabilities of every
test lie in `[0, 1]` (`statClose_iff`, `uprob_nonneg`, `uprob_le_one`). -/
theorem statClose_one (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) : StatClose X Y 1 :=
  (statClose_iff X Y 1).2 fun T => by
    rw [abs_le]
    constructor <;> linarith [uprob_nonneg (fun s => T (X s)), uprob_le_one (fun s => T (X s)),
      uprob_nonneg (fun t => T (Y t)), uprob_le_one (fun t => T (Y t))]

/-- The statistical-switch lemma (C10 of the Chapter 2 inventory): replacing a sampler by a
`δ`-close one changes the success probability of any experiment that also uses independent
auxiliary coins `r : ρ` by at most `δ`. [Gar26, Lemma 3.1] in the sup-over-test-sets form.

**Proof sketch.** Average over the coins `r` (`uprob_prod` after swapping the coordinates):
for fixed `r` the event is the test set `P · r`, whose probability moves by at most `δ`
(`h`); the absolute value of an average is at most the average of the absolute values. -/
theorem StatClose.abs_uprob_sub_le_prod {ρ : Type*} [Fintype ρ] {X : σ → γ} {Y : τ → γ} {δ : ℝ}
    (h : StatClose X Y δ) (P : γ → ρ → Prop) :
    |uprob (fun z : σ × ρ => P (X z.1) z.2) - uprob (fun z : τ × ρ => P (Y z.1) z.2)| ≤ δ := by
  have e1 := uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm ρ σ) (fun z : σ × ρ => P (X z.1) z.2)
  have e2 := uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm ρ τ) (fun z : τ × ρ => P (Y z.1) z.2)
  rw [← e1, ← e2, uprob_prod, uprob_prod]
  exact abs_uexp_sub_le h.nonneg fun r => h fun g => P g r

/-- The distinguishing advantage of any distinguisher `D` (with its own coins) between two
`δ`-close samplers is at most `δ`: the computational counterpart of the statistical
distance bound `distAdv_le_statDist` [Gar26, Lemma 3.1], in the form used by every
"replace the ideal sampler by the rejection sampler" step of the campaign (C10). -/
theorem distAdv_le_of_statClose {σ τ γ ρ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ] [Fintype ρ]
    (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) {δ : ℝ} (h : StatClose X Y δ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y D ≤ δ := by
  unfold distAdv acceptProb
  exact h.abs_uprob_sub_le_prod fun g r => D g r = true

/-- Closeness bounds add under independent products: if `X` is `δ`-close to `X'` and `Y` is
`δ'`-close to `Y'` then the pair sampler `(X, Y)` is `(δ + δ')`-close to `(X', Y')`.

**Proof sketch.** Hybrid `(X', Y)`: the first switch `(X, Y) → (X', Y)` is
`StatClose.abs_uprob_sub_le_prod` for `X, X'` with the second coordinate as auxiliary coins;
the second switch `(X', Y) → (X', Y')` is the same lemma for `Y, Y'` after swapping the
coordinates; conclude by the triangle inequality. -/
theorem StatClose.prod {σ σ' τ τ' γ γ' : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype σ'] [Fintype τ] [Fintype τ']
    {X : σ → γ} {X' : τ → γ} {Y : σ' → γ'} {Y' : τ' → γ'} {δ δ' : ℝ}
    (h : StatClose X X' δ) (h' : StatClose Y Y' δ') :
    StatClose (fun z : σ × σ' => (X z.1, Y z.2)) (fun z : τ × τ' => (X' z.1, Y' z.2)) (δ + δ') := by
  intro T
  have h1 := h.abs_uprob_sub_le_prod fun g s' => T (g, Y s')
  have h2 := h'.abs_uprob_sub_le_prod fun g t => T (X' t, g)
  rw [← uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm τ σ') (fun z : σ' × τ => T (X' z.2, Y z.1)),
    ← uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm τ τ') (fun z : τ' × τ => T (X' z.2, Y' z.1))] at h2
  exact (abs_sub_le _ (uprob fun z : τ × σ' => T (X' z.1, Y z.2)) _).trans (add_le_add h1 h2)

end StatClose

/-! ### Equal fibres push uniform to uniform (C5) -/

/-- A map all of whose fibres have the same positive size `c` pushes the uniform distribution
forward to the uniform distribution (lemma C5 of the Chapter 2 inventory): sampling `QR_N` by
squaring a uniform unit, the squaring map being `4`-to-`1` on `Z_N^*` for `N = pq`
[PS10, Corollary 60.6, Theorem 63.10 (3)].

**Proof sketch.** Group the sum of `F ∘ π` by fibres: every fibre contributes `c · F g`, so
`∑ F ∘ π = c ∑ F` and `|Ω| = c |γ|`; the factor `c` cancels in the average. -/
theorem pushesUniform_of_card_fiber {Ω γ : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ]
    (π : Ω → γ) {c : ℕ} (hc : 0 < c)
    (hfib : ∀ g : γ, (univ.filter fun ω => π ω = g).card = c) : HardcoreBit.PushesUniform π := by
  intro F
  have hsum : ∑ ω, F (π ω) = (c : ℝ) * ∑ g, F g := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_fiberwise' univ π F, mul_sum]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun g _ => ?_
    rw [sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hfib]
  have hcard : Fintype.card Ω = c * Fintype.card γ := by
    rw [← card_univ, card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := π) (t := univ) (fun _ _ => mem_univ _)]
    simp only [hfib, sum_const, card_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
  have hpos : (c : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hc.ne'
  simp only [uexp, hsum, hcard, Nat.cast_mul]
  rw [mul_div_mul_left _ _ hpos]

/-- Pigeonhole for fibres: if every fibre of `π` has at most `c` elements and the domain has
exactly `c` times as many elements as the codomain, then every fibre has exactly `c`
elements (the counting form of "`4`-to-`1`" in [PS10, Corollary 60.6]).

**Proof sketch.** `|Ω| = ∑_g |π⁻¹ g|`; a single fibre below `c` makes the sum below `c |γ|`. -/
theorem card_fiber_eq_of_le {Ω γ : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] (π : Ω → γ)
    {c : ℕ} (hle : ∀ g : γ, (univ.filter fun ω => π ω = g).card ≤ c)
    (hcard : Fintype.card Ω = c * Fintype.card γ) (g : γ) :
    (univ.filter fun ω => π ω = g).card = c := by
  by_contra hne
  have hlt : (univ.filter fun ω => π ω = g).card < c := lt_of_le_of_ne (hle g) hne
  have h1 : Fintype.card Ω = ∑ g, (univ.filter fun ω => π ω = g).card := by
    rw [← card_univ, card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := π) (t := univ) (fun _ _ => mem_univ _)]
  have h2 : ∑ g, (univ.filter fun ω => π ω = g).card < ∑ _g : γ, c :=
    sum_lt_sum (fun g _ => hle g) ⟨g, mem_univ _, hlt⟩
  rw [sum_const, card_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm] at h2
  omega

/-- The `4`-to-`1` form of C5: fibres of size at most `c` and `|Ω| = c |γ|` give a map pushing
uniform to uniform. -/
theorem pushesUniform_of_card_fiber_le {Ω γ : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ]
    (π : Ω → γ) {c : ℕ} (hc : 0 < c) (hle : ∀ g : γ, (univ.filter fun ω => π ω = g).card ≤ c)
    (hcard : Fintype.card Ω = c * Fintype.card γ) : HardcoreBit.PushesUniform π :=
  pushesUniform_of_card_fiber π hc (card_fiber_eq_of_le π hle hcard)

/-! ### Bit strings as numbers -/

/-- The number with the given binary digits (most significant first). -/
def bitsToNat {k : ℕ} (b : Fin k → Bool) : ℕ :=
  (List.ofFn b).foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) 0

/-- **The binary fold with an accumulator**: the fold of `listToNat` started at `a` is
`a · 2^{|l|}` plus the fold started at `0`,
`foldl (a ↦ c ↦ 2a + [c]) a l = a · 2^{|l|} + foldl (a ↦ c ↦ 2a + [c]) 0 l`. -/
theorem foldl_bits_eq (l : List Bool) (a : ℕ) :
    l.foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) a =
      a * 2 ^ l.length + l.foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) 0 := by
  induction l generalizing a with
  | nil => simp
  | cons c l ih =>
    rw [List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_cons, ih, ih (2 * 0 + _), List.length_cons, pow_succ]
    ring

/-- The number read from `l` is below `2^{|l|}`. -/
private theorem listToNat_lt (l : List Bool) :
    l.foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) 0 < 2 ^ l.length := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons c l ih =>
    rw [List.foldl_cons, foldl_bits_eq, List.length_cons, pow_succ]
    cases c <;> simp <;> omega

/-- Lists of the same length reading as the same number are equal. -/
private theorem listToNat_inj : ∀ (l l' : List Bool), l.length = l'.length →
    l.foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) 0 =
      l'.foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) 0 → l = l'
  | [], [], _, _ => rfl
  | c :: l, c' :: l', hlen, heq => by
    rw [List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_cons, foldl_bits_eq, foldl_bits_eq (a := 2 * 0 + _)] at heq
    have hlen' : l.length = l'.length := by simpa using hlen
    have h1 := listToNat_lt l
    have h2 := listToNat_lt l'
    rw [hlen'] at heq h1
    obtain ⟨hc, hl⟩ : c = c' ∧ l.foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) 0 =
        l'.foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) 0 := by
      cases c <;> cases c' <;> simp at heq ⊢ <;> omega
    subst hc
    rw [listToNat_inj l l' hlen' hl]

/-- A `k`-bit string reads as a number below `2^k`. -/
theorem bitsToNat_lt {k : ℕ} (b : Fin k → Bool) : bitsToNat b < 2 ^ k := by
  have := listToNat_lt (List.ofFn b)
  rwa [List.length_ofFn] at this

/-- Reading `k`-bit strings as numbers is injective. -/
theorem bitsToNat_injective {k : ℕ} : Function.Injective (bitsToNat (k := k)) := fun b b' h =>
  List.ofFn_injective (listToNat_inj _ _ (by simp) h)

/-- The bijection between `k`-bit strings and `Fin (2^k)` given by `bitsToNat`: a uniform
`k`-bit string is a uniform number below `2^k`. -/
noncomputable def bitsEquiv (k : ℕ) : (Fin k → Bool) ≃ Fin (2 ^ k) :=
  Equiv.ofBijective (fun b => ⟨bitsToNat b, bitsToNat_lt b⟩)
    ((Fintype.bijective_iff_injective_and_card _).2
      ⟨fun b b' h => bitsToNat_injective (by simpa using congrArg Fin.val h), by simp⟩)

/-- The value of `bitsEquiv` is `bitsToNat`. -/
@[simp] theorem bitsEquiv_val {k : ℕ} (b : Fin k → Bool) : (bitsEquiv k b).val = bitsToNat b :=
  rfl

/-- A uniform `k`-bit string reads as a number below `m ≤ 2^k` with probability `m / 2^k`.

**Proof sketch.** Transport along `bitsEquiv` to the uniform distribution on `Fin (2^k)`,
where the event `{x < m}` has exactly `m` elements. -/
theorem uprob_bitsToNat_lt {m k : ℕ} (hk : m ≤ 2 ^ k) :
    uprob (fun b : Fin k → Bool => bitsToNat b < m) = m / 2 ^ k := by
  let e : {x : Fin (2 ^ k) // x.val < m} ≃ Fin m :=
    { toFun := fun x => ⟨x.1.val, x.2⟩
      invFun := fun y => ⟨⟨y.val, lt_of_lt_of_le y.2 hk⟩, y.2⟩
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl
      right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  rw [show (fun b : Fin k → Bool => bitsToNat b < m) = fun b => (bitsEquiv k b).val < m from rfl,
    uprob_comp_equiv (bitsEquiv k) (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m), uprob, Fintype.card_fin,
    Nat.card_congr e, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Fintype.card_fin]
  push_cast
  rfl

/-- **A positive number is at least half the next power of two**: for `0 < m`,
`2 ^ Nat.size m ≤ 2 m` (the top bit of `m` is bit `size m − 1`: `Nat.lt_size`, `Nat.size_pos`). -/
theorem two_pow_size_le_two_mul {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : 2 ^ Nat.size m ≤ 2 * m := by
  have hpos : 0 < Nat.size m := Nat.size_pos.2 hm
  have h1 : 2 ^ (Nat.size m - 1) ≤ m := Nat.lt_size.1 (Nat.sub_lt hpos one_pos)
  calc 2 ^ Nat.size m = 2 * 2 ^ (Nat.size m - 1) := by
        rw [← pow_succ', Nat.sub_add_cancel hpos]
    _ ≤ 2 * m := Nat.mul_le_mul_left 2 h1

/-- One rejection trial: `k` bits read as a number, accepted iff below `m`. -/
def uniformFromBits (m k : ℕ) (b : Fin k → Bool) : Option (Fin m) :=
  if h : bitsToNat b < m then some ⟨_, h⟩ else none

/-- A trial yields `i` exactly when the bits read as `i`. -/
theorem uniformFromBits_eq_some_iff {m k : ℕ} (b : Fin k → Bool) (i : Fin m) :
    uniformFromBits m k b = some i ↔ bitsToNat b = i.val := by
  unfold uniformFromBits
  split_ifs with h
  · simp [Fin.ext_iff]
  · simp only [false_iff]
    exact fun h' => h (h' ▸ i.isLt)

/-- A trial fails exactly when the bits read as a number `≥ m`. -/
theorem uniformFromBits_eq_none_iff {m k : ℕ} (b : Fin k → Bool) :
    uniformFromBits m k b = none ↔ m ≤ bitsToNat b := by
  unfold uniformFromBits
  split_ifs with h
  · simp [h]
  · simp only [true_iff]
    exact not_lt.1 h

/-- Each value `i : Fin m` is hit by one trial with probability `1 / 2^k` (for `m ≤ 2^k`). -/
theorem uprob_uniformFromBits_eq_some {m k : ℕ} (hk : m ≤ 2 ^ k) (i : Fin m) :
    uprob (fun b : Fin k → Bool => uniformFromBits m k b = some i) = 1 / 2 ^ k := by
  have key := uprob_comp_equiv (bitsEquiv k)
    (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x = ⟨i.val, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 hk⟩)
  rw [OneWay.uprob_eq_one_div_card, Fintype.card_fin] at key
  have hiff : ∀ b : Fin k → Bool,
      uniformFromBits m k b = some i ↔ bitsEquiv k b = ⟨i.val, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 hk⟩ := by
    intro b
    rw [uniformFromBits_eq_some_iff, Fin.ext_iff, bitsEquiv_val]
  rw [OneWay.uprob_congr hiff, key]
  push_cast
  rfl

/-- One trial fails with probability `1 - m / 2^k` (for `m ≤ 2^k`). -/
theorem uprob_uniformFromBits_none {m k : ℕ} (hk : m ≤ 2 ^ k) :
    uprob (fun b : Fin k → Bool => uniformFromBits m k b = none) = 1 - m / 2 ^ k := by
  rw [OneWay.uprob_congr fun b => (uniformFromBits_eq_none_iff b).trans not_lt.symm, uprob_not,
    uprob_bitsToNat_lt hk]

/-- Partition of an event by the value of a map: the probability that `f ω` satisfies `S` is
the sum over `b ∈ S` of the probabilities of the fibres `{f = b}`. -/
theorem uprob_comp_eq_sum_fiber {Ω β : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] (f : Ω → β)
    (S : β → Prop) [DecidablePred S] :
    uprob (fun ω => S (f ω)) = ∑ b ∈ univ.filter S, uprob (fun ω => f ω = b) := by
  simp_rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, ← sum_div]
  congr 1
  rw [card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := f) (s := univ.filter fun ω => S (f ω))
    (t := univ.filter S) (fun ω hω => by simpa using hω)]
  push_cast
  refine sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
  have : (univ.filter fun ω => S (f ω)).filter (fun ω => f ω = b) =
      univ.filter fun ω => f ω = b := by
    ext ω
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, and_iff_right_iff_imp]
    intro h
    rw [h]
    exact (mem_filter.1 hb).2
  rw [this]

/-! ### The first hit of independent draws (C4) -/

/-- The first of the `T` draws `xs 0, …, xs (T-1)` satisfying `E`, if any: the general form of
the rejection sampler (lemma C4 of the Chapter 2 inventory; `SamplePrime`
[PS10, Algorithm 50.16] is `firstHit Prime` on `n`-bit numbers). -/
def firstHit {α : Type*} (E : α → Prop) [DecidablePred E] {T : ℕ} (xs : Fin T → α) : Option α :=
  (List.finRange T).findSome? fun t => if E (xs t) then some (xs t) else none

section FirstHit

variable {α : Type*} (E : α → Prop) [DecidablePred E] {T : ℕ}

/-- The defining equation of `firstHit`: the first draw satisfying `E`,
`firstHit E xs = (List.finRange T).findSome? fun t => if E (xs t) then some (xs t) else none`. -/
theorem firstHit_eq (xs : Fin T → α) :
    firstHit E xs = (List.finRange T).findSome? fun t => if E (xs t) then some (xs t) else none :=
  rfl

/-- No hit exactly when no draw satisfies `E`. -/
theorem firstHit_eq_none_iff (xs : Fin T → α) : firstHit E xs = none ↔ ∀ t, ¬ E (xs t) := by
  unfold firstHit
  rw [List.findSome?_eq_none_iff]
  simp [List.mem_finRange]

/-- A hit satisfies `E`. -/
theorem firstHit_eq_some_imp {xs : Fin T → α} {a : α} (h : firstHit E xs = some a) : E a := by
  unfold firstHit at h
  rw [List.findSome?_eq_some_iff] at h
  obtain ⟨_, t, _, _, ht, _⟩ := h
  by_cases hE : E (xs t)
  · rw [if_pos hE, Option.some.injEq] at ht
    exact ht ▸ hE
  · rw [if_neg hE] at ht
    exact absurd ht (Option.noConfusion)

variable [Fintype α]

/-- `T` independent uniform draws all miss `E` with probability `(1 - Pr[E])^T`
(C4, the failure probability of `SamplePrime` [PS10, Lemma 51.17]). -/
theorem uprob_firstHit_none [Nonempty α] (T : ℕ) :
    uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => firstHit E xs = none) = (1 - uprob E) ^ T := by
  rw [OneWay.uprob_congr fun xs => firstHit_eq_none_iff E xs,
    OneWay.uprob_pi_forall fun a => ¬ E a, Fintype.card_fin, uprob_not]

/-- The first hit is uniform on `E` conditioned on existence: any two elements of `E` are the
first hit with the same probability (C4, [PS10, Lemma 51.17], "`p` is uniform in `Π_n`").

**Proof sketch.** The transposition `s = swap a a'` of `α` preserves `E` (both points lie in
`E`), hence commutes with `firstHit`: `firstHit E (s ∘ xs) = s <$> firstHit E xs`
(`List.map_findSome?`). Applying `s` coordinatewise is a bijection of the draw space
(`uprob_comp_equiv`), and it maps the event `{first hit = a}` onto `{first hit = a'}`. -/
theorem firstHit_uniform_of_some [DecidableEq α] (T : ℕ) {a a' : α} (ha : E a) (ha' : E a') :
    uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => firstHit E xs = some a) =
      uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => firstHit E xs = some a') := by
  have hE : ∀ x, E (Equiv.swap a a' x) ↔ E x := by
    intro x
    by_cases hx : x = a
    · subst hx
      rw [Equiv.swap_apply_left]
      exact ⟨fun _ => ha, fun _ => ha'⟩
    by_cases hx' : x = a'
    · subst hx'
      rw [Equiv.swap_apply_right]
      exact ⟨fun _ => ha', fun _ => ha⟩
    rw [Equiv.swap_apply_of_ne_of_ne hx hx']
  have hmap : ∀ xs : Fin T → α,
      firstHit E (fun t => Equiv.swap a a' (xs t)) = (firstHit E xs).map (Equiv.swap a a') := by
    intro xs
    unfold firstHit
    rw [List.map_findSome?]
    congr 1
    funext t
    by_cases h : E (xs t)
    · simp [h, (hE _).2 h]
    · simp [h, mt (hE _).1 h]
  rw [← uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.piCongrRight fun _ : Fin T => Equiv.swap a a')
    (fun xs => firstHit E xs = some a')]
  refine OneWay.uprob_congr fun xs => ?_
  show firstHit E xs = some a ↔ firstHit E (fun t => Equiv.swap a a' (xs t)) = some a'
  rw [hmap, Option.map_eq_some_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨a, h, Equiv.swap_apply_left a a'⟩
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, hxa⟩
    have hxa' : x = a :=
      (Equiv.swap a a').injective (hxa.trans (Equiv.swap_apply_left a a').symm)
    rw [← hxa']
    exact hx

/-- Falling back to a default element `d ∈ E` when no draw hits makes the first-hit sampler
a total sampler within `(1 - Pr[E])^T` of the uniform distribution on `E` (C4 in the form
consumed by the collections and `SamplePrime`, [PS10, Lemma 51.17]).

**Proof sketch.** Let `f = (1 - Pr[E])^T` be the no-hit probability (`uprob_firstHit_none`)
and `q` the common probability of `{first hit = a}` for `a ∈ E` (`firstHit_uniform_of_some`);
the events `{first hit = a}` (`a ∈ E`) and `{no hit}` partition the draw space, so
`|E| q + f = 1`. For a test set `S`, `Pr[getD d ∈ S] = |S ∩ E| q + [d ∈ S] f` and the ideal
probability is `|S ∩ E| / |E| = |S ∩ E| q + (|S ∩ E| / |E|) f`; both lie in
`[|S ∩ E| q, |S ∩ E| q + f]`, so they differ by at most `f`. Sub-obligations: additivity of
`uprob` over the fibres of `firstHit` (`uprob_eq_card_filter` and
`Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise`), `Fintype.sum_option`, and `uprob` on the subtype
`{a // E a}` as a count (`uprob_eq_card_filter`). -/
theorem statClose_firstHit [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (T : ℕ) {d : α} (hd : E d) :
    StatClose (fun xs : Fin T → α => (firstHit E xs).getD d) (fun e : {a // E a} => (e : α))
      ((1 - uprob E) ^ T) := by
  classical
  intro S
  have hsome : ∀ a, E a → uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => firstHit E xs = some a) =
      uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => firstHit E xs = some d) :=
    fun a ha => firstHit_uniform_of_some E T ha hd
  have hnot : ∀ a, ¬ E a → uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => firstHit E xs = some a) = 0 := by
    intro a ha
    rw [← uprob_false (α := Fin T → α)]
    exact OneWay.uprob_congr fun xs => ⟨fun h => ha (firstHit_eq_some_imp E h), False.elim⟩
  -- the law of `firstHit`: `none` with probability `f`, each `a ∈ E` with probability `q`
  have hdec : ∀ S' : Option α → Prop, uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => S' (firstHit E xs)) =
      (if S' none then (1 - uprob E) ^ T else 0) +
        uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => firstHit E xs = some d) *
          (univ.filter fun a => E a ∧ S' (some a)).card := by
    intro S'
    rw [uprob_comp_eq_sum_fiber (firstHit E) S', sum_filter, Fintype.sum_option,
      uprob_firstHit_none E T]
    congr 1
    rw [mul_comm, ← nsmul_eq_mul, ← sum_const, sum_filter]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    by_cases hSa : S' (some a)
    · by_cases hEa : E a
      · simp [hSa, hEa, hsome a hEa]
      · simp [hSa, hEa, hnot a hEa]
    · simp [hSa]
  have h1 := hdec fun o => S (o.getD d)
  simp only [Option.getD_none, Option.getD_some] at h1
  have htot := hdec fun _ => True
  simp only [uprob_true, if_true, and_true] at htot
  have hideal : uprob (fun e : {a // E a} => S e.val) =
      ((univ.filter fun a => E a ∧ S a).card : ℝ) / (univ.filter E).card := by
    rw [uprob, Nat.card_congr (Equiv.subtypeSubtypeEquivSubtypeInter E S), Nat.card_eq_fintype_card,
      Fintype.card_subtype, Fintype.card_subtype]
  rw [h1, hideal]
  -- arithmetic: with `N = |E|`, `M = |E ∩ S|`, `q N = 1 - f`, the difference is `f ([d ∈ S] - M/N)`
  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < (univ.filter E).card := by
    exact_mod_cast card_pos.2 ⟨d, by simpa using hd⟩
  have hMN : ((univ.filter fun a => E a ∧ S a).card : ℝ) ≤ (univ.filter E).card := by
    exact_mod_cast card_le_card fun a ha => by
      simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and] at ha ⊢
      exact ha.1
  have hf0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (1 - uprob E) ^ T := pow_nonneg (by linarith [uprob_le_one E]) T
  have hq : uprob (fun xs : Fin T → α => firstHit E xs = some d) =
      (1 - (1 - uprob E) ^ T) / (univ.filter E).card := by
    rw [eq_div_iff hN.ne']
    linarith
  rw [hq]
  have hr0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((univ.filter fun a => E a ∧ S a).card : ℝ) / (univ.filter E).card :=
    div_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) hN.le
  have hr1 : ((univ.filter fun a => E a ∧ S a).card : ℝ) / (univ.filter E).card ≤ 1 :=
    (div_le_one hN).2 hMN
  have hrw : (1 - (1 - uprob E) ^ T) / (univ.filter E).card *
      ((univ.filter fun a => E a ∧ S a).card : ℝ) =
      (1 - (1 - uprob E) ^ T) *
        (((univ.filter fun a => E a ∧ S a).card : ℝ) / (univ.filter E).card) := by
    ring
  rw [hrw]
  generalize ((univ.filter fun a => E a ∧ S a).card : ℝ) / (univ.filter E).card = r at hr0 hr1 ⊢
  generalize (1 - uprob E) ^ T = f at hf0 ⊢
  by_cases hSd : S d
  · rw [if_pos hSd]
    exact abs_le.2 ⟨by nlinarith, by nlinarith⟩
  · rw [if_neg hSd]
    exact abs_le.2 ⟨by nlinarith, by nlinarith⟩

end FirstHit

/-! ### Rejection sampling of `Fin m` -/

/-- `T` rejection trials of `k` bits each; the first accepted value. Uniform on `Fin m`
conditioned on `some`; `none` with probability `(1 - m/2^k)^T`. The sampler of the uniform
position `i ∈ [m]` of [PS10, Theorem 35.1] and of the residues of [PS10, §2.6–§2.12]. -/
def rejectionSample (m k T : ℕ) (b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool) : Option (Fin m) :=
  (List.finRange T).findSome? fun t => uniformFromBits m k (b t)

/-- The rejection sampler fails exactly when every trial fails. -/
theorem rejectionSample_eq_none_iff (m k T : ℕ) (b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool) :
    rejectionSample m k T b = none ↔ ∀ t, uniformFromBits m k (b t) = none := by
  unfold rejectionSample
  rw [List.findSome?_eq_none_iff]
  simp [List.mem_finRange]

/-- The rejection sampler is the first hit of the event `{x < m}` among the `T` numbers read
from the trials (embedding `Fin m` into `Fin (2^k)`). -/
theorem map_rejectionSample_eq_firstHit {m k T : ℕ} (hk : m ≤ 2 ^ k) (b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool) :
    (rejectionSample m k T b).map (fun i : Fin m => (⟨i.val, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 hk⟩ : Fin (2 ^ k))) =
      firstHit (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) (fun t => bitsEquiv k (b t)) := by
  unfold rejectionSample firstHit
  rw [List.map_findSome?]
  congr 1
  funext t
  simp only [Function.comp, uniformFromBits, bitsEquiv_val]
  split_ifs <;> rfl

/-- Lemma C4 for the rejection sampler: conditioned on success the output is uniform — any two
values of `Fin m` are output with the same probability ([PS10, Theorem 35.1], the uniform
position; [PS10, Lemma 51.17]).

**Proof sketch.** By `map_rejectionSample_eq_firstHit` the event `{output = i}` is the event
`{firstHit {x < m} = i}` for the numbers read from the trials; reading is a bijection of
each trial's bits onto `Fin (2^k)` (`bitsEquiv`, applied coordinatewise by
`Equiv.piCongrRight`), and `firstHit_uniform_of_some` gives the symmetry between `i` and
`j`. -/
theorem rejectionSample_uniform_of_some (m k T : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hk : m ≤ 2 ^ k) (i j : Fin m) :
    uprob (fun b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool => rejectionSample m k T b = some i) =
      uprob (fun b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool => rejectionSample m k T b = some j) := by
  have _ := hm
  let toBig : Fin m → Fin (2 ^ k) := fun i => ⟨i.val, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 hk⟩
  have hinj : Function.Injective toBig := fun x y h =>
    Fin.ext (show (toBig x).val = (toBig y).val from congrArg Fin.val h)
  have key : ∀ (b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool) (i : Fin m), rejectionSample m k T b = some i ↔
      firstHit (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) (fun t => bitsEquiv k (b t)) = some (toBig i) := by
    intro b i
    rw [← map_rejectionSample_eq_firstHit hk, Option.map_eq_some_iff]
    constructor
    · intro h
      exact ⟨i, h, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨x, hx, hxi⟩
      rw [hinj hxi] at hx
      exact hx
  have e : ∀ i : Fin m, uprob (fun b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool =>
      firstHit (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) (fun t => bitsEquiv k (b t)) = some (toBig i)) =
      uprob (fun xs : Fin T → Fin (2 ^ k) =>
        firstHit (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) xs = some (toBig i)) := fun i =>
    uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.piCongrRight fun _ : Fin T => bitsEquiv k)
      (fun xs => firstHit (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) xs = some (toBig i))
  rw [OneWay.uprob_congr fun b => key b i, OneWay.uprob_congr fun b => key b j, e i, e j]
  exact firstHit_uniform_of_some _ T i.2 j.2

/-- The rejection sampler fails with probability exactly `(1 - m/2^k)^T` (C4, the no-hit
probability; [PS10, Lemma 51.17] with `Pr[E] = m/2^k`). -/
theorem uprob_rejectionSample_none (m k T : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hk : m ≤ 2 ^ k) :
    uprob (fun b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool => rejectionSample m k T b = none) =
      (1 - (m : ℝ) / 2 ^ k) ^ T := by
  have _ := hm
  rw [OneWay.uprob_congr fun b => rejectionSample_eq_none_iff m k T b,
    OneWay.uprob_pi_forall fun c : Fin k → Bool => uniformFromBits m k c = none,
    Fintype.card_fin, uprob_uniformFromBits_none hk]

/-- With `k` chosen so that `2^k ≤ 2m` (the smallest `k` with `m ≤ 2^k`), every trial fails
with probability at most `1/2`, so `T` trials fail with probability at most `2^{-T}`: the
choice of `T = n` in the campaign's honest samplers. -/
theorem uprob_rejectionSample_none_le_half_pow (m k T : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hk : m ≤ 2 ^ k)
    (h2 : 2 ^ k ≤ 2 * m) :
    uprob (fun b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool => rejectionSample m k T b = none) ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ T := by
  rw [uprob_rejectionSample_none m k T hm hk]
  have h2k : (0 : ℝ) < 2 ^ k := by positivity
  have hm' : (m : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ k := by exact_mod_cast hk
  have h2' : (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ 2 * m := by exact_mod_cast h2
  apply pow_le_pow_left₀
  · rw [sub_nonneg, div_le_one h2k]
    exact hm'
  · have : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ m / 2 ^ k := by
      rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (by norm_num) h2k]
      linarith
    linarith

/-- `(1 - 1/m)^m ≤ 1/2` for `m ≥ 1`: `m` trials each failing with probability `1 - 1/m`
all fail with probability at most `1/2` (the dyadic form of "`(1 - 1/m)^m ≈ e^{-1}`").

**Proof sketch.** Bernoulli's inequality `one_add_mul_le_pow` gives `(1 + 1/m)^m ≥ 2`, and
`(1 - 1/m)^m (1 + 1/m)^m = (1 - 1/m²)^m ≤ 1`, so `(1 - 1/m)^m ≤ 1/(1 + 1/m)^m ≤ 1/2`. -/
theorem one_sub_inv_pow_le_half (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : (1 - 1 / (m : ℝ)) ^ m ≤ 1 / 2 := by
  have hm' : (0 : ℝ) < m := by exact_mod_cast hm
  set x : ℝ := 1 / m with hx
  have hx0 : 0 ≤ x := by positivity
  have hx1 : x ≤ 1 := by
    rw [hx, div_le_one hm']
    exact_mod_cast hm
  have hb : 1 + (m : ℝ) * x ≤ (1 + x) ^ m := one_add_mul_le_pow (by linarith) m
  have hmx : (m : ℝ) * x = 1 := by
    rw [hx]
    field_simp
  rw [hmx] at hb
  have hprod : (1 - x) ^ m * (1 + x) ^ m ≤ 1 := by
    rw [← mul_pow]
    have : (1 - x) * (1 + x) = 1 - x ^ 2 := by ring
    rw [this]
    exact pow_le_one₀ (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith)
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < (1 + x) ^ m := by positivity
  calc (1 - x) ^ m = (1 - x) ^ m * (1 + x) ^ m / (1 + x) ^ m := by field_simp
    _ ≤ 1 / (1 + x) ^ m := by gcongr
    _ ≤ 1 / 2 := one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by norm_num) (by linarith)

/-- Fallback-to-default makes a total sampler within `(1 - m/2^k)^T` of uniform: the form of
C4 consumed by Theorem 35.1 (uniform position), the collections (`SampleClose`) and the
Chapter 4 simulators.

**Proof sketch.** Let `f = (1 - m/2^k)^T` (`uprob_rejectionSample_none`) and `q` the common
probability of `{output = i}` (`rejectionSample_uniform_of_some`); the `m + 1` events
`{output = i}`, `{output = none}` partition the coin space, so `m q + f = 1`. For a test set
`S ⊆ Fin m`, `Pr[getD d ∈ S] = |S| q + [d ∈ S] f` and `|S| / m = |S| q + (|S|/m) f`; both lie
in `[|S| q, |S| q + f]`. Alternatively: `map_rejectionSample_eq_firstHit`, the coordinatewise
bijection `bitsEquiv`, and `statClose_firstHit` on `Fin (2^k)` with `E = {x < m}`, transported
along the bijection `{x : Fin (2^k) // x < m} ≃ Fin m` (`StatClose.comp_equiv_right`,
`StatClose.map`). -/
theorem statClose_rejectionSample (m k T : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hk : m ≤ 2 ^ k) (d : Fin m) :
    StatClose (fun b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool => (rejectionSample m k T b).getD d) (id : Fin m → Fin m)
      ((1 - (m : ℝ) / 2 ^ k) ^ T) := by
  have _ := hm
  let toBig : Fin m → Fin (2 ^ k) := fun i => ⟨i.val, lt_of_lt_of_le i.2 hk⟩
  let g : Fin (2 ^ k) → Fin m := fun x => if h : x.val < m then ⟨x.val, h⟩ else d
  let e : Fin m ≃ {x : Fin (2 ^ k) // x.val < m} :=
    { toFun := fun i => ⟨toBig i, i.2⟩
      invFun := fun x => ⟨x.1.val, x.2⟩
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl
      right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  have hE : uprob (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) = m / 2 ^ k := by
    rw [← uprob_bitsToNat_lt hk, ← uprob_comp_equiv (bitsEquiv k) (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m)]
    rfl
  have h := (((statClose_firstHit (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) T (d := toBig d) d.2).comp_equiv_left
    (Equiv.piCongrRight fun _ : Fin T => bitsEquiv k)).map g).comp_equiv_right e
  rw [hE] at h
  have h' : StatClose (fun b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool =>
      g ((firstHit (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) (fun t => bitsEquiv k (b t))).getD (toBig d)))
      (fun i : Fin m => g (toBig i)) ((1 - (m : ℝ) / 2 ^ k) ^ T) := h
  have hX : (fun b : Fin T → Fin k → Bool =>
      g ((firstHit (fun x : Fin (2 ^ k) => x.val < m) (fun t => bitsEquiv k (b t))).getD (toBig d))) =
      fun b => (rejectionSample m k T b).getD d := by
    funext b
    rw [← map_rejectionSample_eq_firstHit hk]
    cases rejectionSample m k T b with
    | none => simp [g, toBig, d.2]
    | some i => simp [g, i.2]
  have hY : (fun i : Fin m => g (toBig i)) = id := by
    funext i
    simp [g, toBig, i.2]
  rw [hX, hY] at h'
  exact h'

/-! ### Total samplers from samplers that are uniform conditioned on success -/

/-- A sampler `S : Ω → Option γ` that is uniform conditioned on success (any two values are
output with the same probability) and fails with probability at most `f`, made total by a
default `d`, is within `f` of the uniform distribution on `γ`: the common argument of
`statClose_firstHit`, `statClose_rejectionSample` and `statClose_permFromCoins` (lemma C4 in
its abstract form; [PS10, Lemma 51.17] for `SamplePrime`, [PS10, Protocol 120.6] for
`π ← S_n`).

**Repair (run-3 audit P2-1):** added so that the permutation sampler has a `StatClose` form
in this file instead of in each consumer.

**Proof sketch.** With `p = Pr[S = none]`, `q = Pr[S = some d]` (the common value of
`Pr[S = some a]`) and `G = |γ|`, the `G + 1` events `{S = some a}`, `{S = none}` partition the
seed space (`uprob_comp_eq_sum_fiber`, `Fintype.sum_option`), so `p + q G = 1`; for a test
set `T` with `M = |T|`, `Pr[getD d ∈ T] = [d ∈ T] p + q M` and `M / G = q M + (M / G) p`,
whose difference is `p ([d ∈ T] - M/G)`, of absolute value at most `p ≤ f`. -/
theorem statClose_getD_of_uniform_of_some {Ω γ : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq γ] (S : Ω → Option γ)
    (huni : ∀ a a' : γ, uprob (fun ω => S ω = some a) = uprob (fun ω => S ω = some a'))
    {f : ℝ} (hf : uprob (fun ω => S ω = none) ≤ f) (d : γ) :
    StatClose (fun ω => (S ω).getD d) (id : γ → γ) f := by
  classical
  intro T
  -- the law of `S`: `none` with probability `p`, each `a : γ` with the common probability `q`
  have hdec : ∀ S' : Option γ → Prop, uprob (fun ω => S' (S ω)) =
      (if S' none then uprob (fun ω => S ω = none) else 0) +
        uprob (fun ω => S ω = some d) * (univ.filter fun a => S' (some a)).card := by
    intro S'
    rw [uprob_comp_eq_sum_fiber S S', sum_filter, Fintype.sum_option]
    congr 1
    rw [mul_comm, ← nsmul_eq_mul, ← sum_const, sum_filter]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    by_cases hSa : S' (some a)
    · simp [hSa, huni a d]
    · simp [hSa]
  have h1 := hdec fun o => T (o.getD d)
  simp only [Option.getD_none, Option.getD_some] at h1
  have htot := hdec fun _ => True
  simp only [uprob_true, if_true, filter_true, card_univ] at htot
  have hideal : uprob (fun a : γ => T (id a)) = ((univ.filter T).card : ℝ) / Fintype.card γ := by
    rw [uprob_eq_card_filter]
    rfl
  rw [h1, hideal]
  -- arithmetic: with `q G = 1 - p`, the difference is `p ([d ∈ T] - M/G)`
  have hG : (0 : ℝ) < Fintype.card γ := by exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_pos_iff.2 ⟨d⟩
  have hMG : ((univ.filter T).card : ℝ) ≤ Fintype.card γ := by
    exact_mod_cast card_le_univ _
  have hp0 : 0 ≤ uprob (fun ω => S ω = none) := uprob_nonneg _
  have hq : uprob (fun ω => S ω = some d) =
      (1 - uprob (fun ω => S ω = none)) / Fintype.card γ := by
    rw [eq_div_iff hG.ne']
    linarith
  rw [hq]
  have hrw : (1 - uprob (fun ω => S ω = none)) / Fintype.card γ * ((univ.filter T).card : ℝ) =
      (1 - uprob (fun ω => S ω = none)) * (((univ.filter T).card : ℝ) / Fintype.card γ) := by
    ring
  rw [hrw]
  have hr0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((univ.filter T).card : ℝ) / Fintype.card γ :=
    div_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) hG.le
  have hr1 : ((univ.filter T).card : ℝ) / Fintype.card γ ≤ 1 := (div_le_one hG).2 hMG
  generalize ((univ.filter T).card : ℝ) / Fintype.card γ = r at hr0 hr1 ⊢
  generalize uprob (fun ω => S ω = none) = p at hp0 hf ⊢
  by_cases hTd : T d
  · rw [if_pos hTd]
    exact abs_le.2 ⟨by nlinarith, by nlinarith⟩
  · rw [if_neg hTd]
    exact abs_le.2 ⟨by nlinarith, by nlinarith⟩

end TCSlib.Cryptography
```

```text
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors

import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePairing
import TCSlib.Cryptography.NumberTheory.Primality
import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Size

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The polynomial-time arithmetic hypothesis bundle

The candidate one-way functions of [PS10, §2.3, §2.7–§2.12] are "easy to compute", "easy to
sample" and their reductions run in polynomial time because binary multiplication, addition,
(truncated) subtraction, division with remainder, the extended Euclidean algorithm
[PS10, Algorithm 43.2], modular exponentiation [PS10, Algorithm 45.5], comparison, the bit
length and primality testing [PS10, §2.6.5, Remark on p. 33 (AKS)] are polynomial-time
computable on binary numerals.
The repository has no machines for binary arithmetic (inventory finding F1), so, by the
campaign's decision (plan `PassShelatChapter2-4Plan.md`, decision log "conditional
candidates", foundation decision D11), these facts are taken as an **explicit hypothesis
bundle** `ArithmeticFP`, never as axioms: every number-theoretic candidate theorem of the
campaign is stated under `H : ArithmeticFP`, and `#print axioms` stays clean.

Conventions. Numbers on tapes are binary numerals, most significant bit first, read by
`TCSlib.Cryptography.NumberTheory.listToNat` (leading zeros allowed) and written in a
prescribed width by `natToList k N` (the `k` low-order bits of `N`, most significant first;
exact when `N < 2^k`). The typed `k`-bit strings `Fin k → Bool` of the experiments are read
by `TCSlib.Cryptography.bitsToNat` and written by `natToBits k N`; the two conventions agree
through `List.ofFn` (`bitsToNat_eq_listToNat`, `natToList`). Arguments of the arithmetic
functions are paired with `Turing.pairEncode`.

**Deviation:** [PS10] treats the arithmetic algorithms as given (§2.6 gives their operation
counts; the `NumberTheory` modules formalize those); here their polynomial-time
computability on strings is a hypothesis, discharged by a future machine-building campaign.

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.natToBits`, `natToList` — fixed-width binary numerals.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.mulStr`, `addStr`, `subStr`, `divModStr`, `xgcdStr`,
  `modExpStr`, `leStr`, `sizeStr`, `primeStr` — the string functions of the bundle
  (`addStr`, `subStr`, `sizeStr` added by the run-3 audit repair P7-1: the reductions of
  §2.9–§2.12 decrement, add and subtract numerals and read bit lengths).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.ArithmeticFP` — the hypothesis bundle (a `Prop`
  structure).

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.listToNat_natToList`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.bitsToNat_natToBits`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.natToBits_bitsToNat` — the encodings are mutually
  inverse on numbers below `2^k`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.natToBits_injOn` — `natToBits k` is injective below `2^k`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.natToList_length_listToNat`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.natToList_val_natCast` — a numeral is the numeral of its
  value at its own width (canonicity of the candidates' decoders).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.listToNat_addStr`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.listToNat_subStr` — addition and truncated subtraction of
  numerals are lossless at the widths of the bundle.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.val_units_pow` — `(x^e).val = x.val^e mod M` in `Z_M^*`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.natToList_mod_two_pow`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.listToNat_natToList_zero_append`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.natToList_zero_append_drop`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.listToNat_replicate_true`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.listToNat_replicate_false` — widths, leading zeros and the
  constant words.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.subStr_self`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.listToNat_mulStr`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.val_inv_natCast_zmod_zero_le` — readings of the bundle's words.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.ArithmeticFP.le_poly`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.ArithmeticFP.prime_poly` — comparisons and primality tests of
  polynomial-time words are polynomial-time.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§2.3 (multiplication), §2.6.1–§2.6.6 (Euclid, modular exponentiation, primality
  testing), Remark on p. 33 (AKS).)
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Cambridge
  University Press, 2009 (the string-function class FP, `Complexity.PolyTimeComputable`).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates

open Complexity Turing NumberTheory

/-! ## Fixed-width binary numerals -/

/-- The `k`-bit binary numeral of `N`, most significant bit first: bit `i` is the
`(k - 1 - i)`-th binary digit of `N` (the `k` low-order digits of `N`; exact when
`N < 2^k`). The inverse of `TCSlib.Cryptography.bitsToNat` on `Fin k → Bool`. -/
def natToBits (k N : ℕ) : Fin k → Bool := fun i => N.testBit (k - 1 - i)

/-- The `k`-bit binary numeral of `N` as a string (most significant bit first). -/
def natToList (k N : ℕ) : List Bool := List.ofFn (natToBits k N)

/-- The defining equation of `natToList`: `natToList k N = List.ofFn (natToBits k N)`, the
string of the `k`-bit numeral of `N`. -/
theorem natToList_eq (k N : ℕ) : natToList k N = List.ofFn (natToBits k N) := rfl

/-- `natToList` has length `k`. -/
@[simp] theorem length_natToList (k N : ℕ) : (natToList k N).length = k := by
  simp [natToList]

/-- The `0`-bit numeral is empty (moved from `RSA.lean`, run-3 audit P7-6). -/
theorem natToList_zero (N : ℕ) : natToList 0 N = [] := by simp [natToList]

/-- Dropping the last bit of a `(k+1)`-bit numeral of `N` gives the `k`-bit numeral of
`N / 2`. -/
theorem natToBits_succ_castSucc (k N : ℕ) (i : Fin k) :
    natToBits (k + 1) N (Fin.castSucc i) = natToBits k (N / 2) i := by
  simp only [natToBits, Fin.coe_castSucc]
  have h : k + 1 - 1 - (i : ℕ) = (k - 1 - i) + 1 := by have := i.2; omega
  rw [h, Nat.testBit_succ]

/-- The last bit of a `(k+1)`-bit numeral of `N` is the parity of `N`. -/
theorem natToBits_succ_last (k N : ℕ) : natToBits (k + 1) N (Fin.last k) = N.testBit 0 := by
  simp [natToBits]

/-- `listToNat` of the `k`-bit numeral of `N` is `N mod 2^k` (the numeral keeps the `k`
low-order digits). -/
theorem listToNat_natToList_eq_mod (k N : ℕ) : listToNat (natToList k N) = N % 2 ^ k := by
  induction k generalizing N with
  | zero => simp [natToList, listToNat_eq, Nat.mod_one]
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [natToList, List.ofFn_succ', List.concat_eq_append]
    simp only [natToBits_succ_castSucc, natToBits_succ_last]
    rw [listToNat_eq, List.foldl_concat, ← listToNat_eq, ← natToList, ih, pow_succ', Nat.mod_mul]
    have h0 : (if N.testBit 0 then 1 else 0) = N % 2 := by
      have := Nat.toNat_testBit N 0
      simp only [pow_zero, Nat.div_one] at this
      rw [← this]
      cases N.testBit 0 <;> rfl
    rw [h0]
    omega

/-- **The encodings are inverse** (reading): `listToNat (natToList k N) = N` for `N < 2^k`. -/
theorem listToNat_natToList {k N : ℕ} (h : N < 2 ^ k) : listToNat (natToList k N) = N := by
  rw [listToNat_natToList_eq_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h]

/-- `bitsToNat` of the `k`-bit numeral of `N` is `N` for `N < 2^k`. -/
theorem bitsToNat_natToBits {k N : ℕ} (h : N < 2 ^ k) : bitsToNat (natToBits k N) = N := by
  rw [bitsToNat_eq_listToNat]
  exact listToNat_natToList h

/-- **The encodings are inverse** (writing): the `k`-bit numeral of `bitsToNat b` is `b`. -/
theorem natToBits_bitsToNat {k : ℕ} (b : Fin k → Bool) : natToBits k (bitsToNat b) = b :=
  bitsToNat_injective (bitsToNat_natToBits (bitsToNat_lt b))

/-- `natToBits k` is injective on numbers below `2^k`. -/
theorem natToBits_injOn {k M N : ℕ} (hM : M < 2 ^ k) (hN : N < 2 ^ k)
    (h : natToBits k M = natToBits k N) : M = N := by
  rw [← bitsToNat_natToBits hM, ← bitsToNat_natToBits hN, h]

/-- `natToList k` is injective on numbers below `2^k`. -/
theorem natToList_injOn {k M N : ℕ} (hM : M < 2 ^ k) (hN : N < 2 ^ k)
    (h : natToList k M = natToList k N) : M = N :=
  natToBits_injOn hM hN (List.ofFn_injective h)

/-- `listToNat` of an `n`-bit string is below `2^n`. -/
theorem listToNat_lt_two_pow (w : List Bool) : listToNat w < 2 ^ w.length := by
  have h := bitsToNat_lt (fun i : Fin w.length => w.get i)
  rw [bitsToNat_eq_listToNat] at h
  simpa using h

/-- **A numeral rewritten at its own width is unchanged**: `natToList |w| (listToNat w) = w`
(the numeral decoders of the candidates are canonical; gate 03b, finding 1). -/
theorem natToList_length_listToNat (w : List Bool) : natToList w.length (listToNat w) = w := by
  have h := natToBits_bitsToNat w.get
  rw [bitsToNat_eq_listToNat, List.ofFn_get] at h
  rw [natToList, h, List.ofFn_get]

/-- **A numeral of width `k` reading below `M` is the `k`-bit numeral of its residue in
`Z_M`**: `natToList k ((listToNat w : Z_M).val) = w` for `|w| = k` and `listToNat w < M`. -/
theorem natToList_val_natCast {k M : ℕ} {w : List Bool} (hk : w.length = k)
    (hM : listToNat w < M) : natToList k ((listToNat w : ZMod M).val) = w := by
  rw [ZMod.val_cast_of_lt hM, ← hk, natToList_length_listToNat]

/-- **A numeral keeps the low bits**: `⟦N mod 2^k⟧_k = ⟦N⟧_k`. -/
theorem natToList_mod_two_pow (k N : ℕ) : natToList k (N % 2 ^ k) = natToList k N := by
  have h := natToList_length_listToNat (natToList k N)
  rw [length_natToList, listToNat_natToList_eq_mod] at h
  exact h

/-- **Leading zeros do not change the value**: `⟦⟦0⟧_k ++ w⟧ = ⟦w⟧`. -/
theorem listToNat_natToList_zero_append (k : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    listToNat (natToList k 0 ++ w) = listToNat w := by
  rw [listToNat_append, listToNat_natToList (Nat.two_pow_pos k), zero_mul, zero_add]

/-- **Width normalization by truncation**: the last `W` bits of `⟦0⟧_W ++ b` are the
`W`-bit numeral of `⟦b⟧`, `(⟦0⟧_W ++ b).drop |b| = ⟦⟦b⟧⟧_W` (the low `W` bits, also when
`⟦b⟧ ≥ 2^W`).

**Proof sketch.** The word `w = ⟦0⟧_W ++ b` reads as `⟦b⟧` (leading zeros), and splitting it after
its first `|b|` bits gives `⟦w⟧ = ⟦w.take |b|⟧ · 2^W + ⟦w.drop |b|⟧` (`listToNat_append`), where the
second summand is below `2^W`. So `⟦w.drop |b|⟧ = ⟦b⟧ mod 2^W`, and a word of length `W` is the
numeral of its value (`natToList_length_listToNat`, `natToList_mod_two_pow`). -/
theorem natToList_zero_append_drop (W : ℕ) (b : List Bool) :
    (natToList W 0 ++ b).drop b.length = natToList W (listToNat b) := by
  set w := natToList W 0 ++ b with hw
  have hlen : (w.drop b.length).length = W := by
    rw [List.length_drop, hw, List.length_append, length_natToList]
    omega
  have hval : listToNat w = listToNat b := listToNat_natToList_zero_append W b
  have hsplit : listToNat w = listToNat (w.take b.length) * 2 ^ W + listToNat (w.drop b.length) := by
    conv_lhs => rw [← List.take_append_drop b.length w]
    rw [listToNat_append, hlen]
  have hlt := listToNat_lt_two_pow (w.drop b.length)
  rw [hlen] at hlt
  have hmod : listToNat b % 2 ^ W = listToNat (w.drop b.length) := by
    rw [← hval, hsplit, Nat.mul_add_mod_of_lt hlt]
  rw [← natToList_mod_two_pow, hmod, ← hlen, natToList_length_listToNat]

/-- **The all-ones word** `1^k` reads as `2^k − 1`: `listToNat (1^k) = 2^k − 1`. -/
theorem listToNat_replicate_true (k : ℕ) : listToNat (List.replicate k true) = 2 ^ k - 1 := by
  induction k with
  | zero => rw [List.replicate_zero, listToNat_nil, pow_zero, Nat.sub_self]
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [List.replicate_succ', listToNat_append, ih, listToNat_singleton_true,
      List.length_singleton, pow_succ]
    have := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := k)
    omega

/-- **The all-zeros word** `0^k` reads as `0`: `listToNat (0^k) = 0`. -/
theorem listToNat_replicate_false (k : ℕ) : listToNat (List.replicate k false) = 0 := by
  induction k with
  | zero => rw [List.replicate_zero, listToNat_nil]
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [List.replicate_succ, listToNat_cons, ih, if_neg Bool.false_ne_true, zero_mul, add_zero]

/-! ## The string functions of the bundle -/

/-- Binary multiplication: `⟨a, b⟩ ↦ a · b` as an `(|a| + |b|)`-bit numeral (lossless: the
product of an `|a|`-bit and a `|b|`-bit number has at most `|a| + |b|` bits). -/
def mulStr (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  natToList ((pairFstD z).length + (pairSndD z).length)
    (listToNat (pairFstD z) * listToNat (pairSndD z))

/-- Binary addition: `⟨a, b⟩ ↦ a + b` as an `(|a| + |b|)`-bit numeral (lossless,
`listToNat_addStr`: `a + b < 2^{|a|} + 2^{|b|} ≤ 2^{|a| + |b|}` when both numerals are nonempty,
and `a + b = b` when `a` is empty). Repair (run-3 audit P7-1): added to the bundle; the
reductions of [PS10, §2.12] add numerals (the CRT sum of Theorem 58.3, the increment
`(p+1)/4`). -/
def addStr (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  natToList ((pairFstD z).length + (pairSndD z).length)
    (listToNat (pairFstD z) + listToNat (pairSndD z))

/-- Truncated subtraction: `⟨a, b⟩ ↦ a ∸ b` (`0` when `b > a`) as an `|a|`-bit numeral
(lossless, `listToNat_subStr`). The decrement `p − 1` of `Φ(N) = (p−1)(q−1)` [PS10, p. 47]
is `subStr ⟨p, [true]⟩`, and `(x − z) mod N` is `(x + (N ∸ (z mod N))) mod N`. Repair (run-3
audit P7-1): added to the bundle. -/
def subStr (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  natToList (pairFstD z).length (listToNat (pairFstD z) - listToNat (pairSndD z))

/-- Bit length: `w ↦ 1^{Nat.size N}` for `N = listToNat w`, the length of the numeral of `N`
with its leading zeros stripped (`Nat.size N = ⌈log₂ (N + 1)⌉`, `N < 2^{Nat.size N} ≤ 2N` for
`N ≥ 1`), written in unary — the form in which lengths drive the cuts
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly`. Repair (run-3 audit P7-1): added to the bundle;
the rejection samplers of [PS10, §2.9–§2.12, §3.x] read `k = Nat.size N` bits per trial. -/
def sizeStr (w : List Bool) : List Bool := List.replicate (Nat.size (listToNat w)) true

/-- Division with remainder: `⟨a, b⟩ ↦ ⟨a / b, a mod b⟩`, the quotient as an `|a|`-bit and
the remainder as a `|b|`-bit numeral (Lean's convention `a / 0 = 0`, `a mod 0 = a`). -/
def divModStr (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (natToList (pairFstD z).length (listToNat (pairFstD z) / listToNat (pairSndD z)))
    (natToList (pairSndD z).length (listToNat (pairFstD z) % listToNat (pairSndD z)))

/-- The extended Euclidean algorithm [PS10, Algorithm 43.2] in the form the candidates use:
`⟨a, b⟩ ↦ ⟨gcd(a, b), a⁻¹ mod b⟩`, both as `|b|`-bit numerals, where `a⁻¹ mod b` is
`ZMod.inv` (the Bézout coefficient of `a` reduced modulo `b`; the inverse of `a` in `Z_b^*`
when `gcd(a, b) = 1`, [PS10, Claim 44.5 and Theorem 46.8]). -/
def xgcdStr (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (natToList (pairSndD z).length (Nat.gcd (listToNat (pairFstD z)) (listToNat (pairSndD z))))
    (natToList (pairSndD z).length
      (ZMod.val ((listToNat (pairFstD z) : ZMod (listToNat (pairSndD z)))⁻¹)))

/-- Modular exponentiation [PS10, Algorithm 45.5]: `⟨a, ⟨x, N⟩⟩ ↦ a^x mod N` as an
`|N|`-bit numeral. -/
def modExpStr (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  natToList (pairSndD (pairSndD z)).length
    (listToNat (pairFstD z) ^ listToNat (pairFstD (pairSndD z)) % listToNat (pairSndD (pairSndD z)))

/-- Comparison: `⟨a, b⟩ ↦ [a ≤ b]`. -/
def leStr (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  [decide (listToNat (pairFstD z) ≤ listToNat (pairSndD z))]

/-- Primality test: `w ↦ [w is prime]` (the hypothesis of
`TCSlib.Cryptography.NumberTheory.exists_samplePrime_nuppt`). -/
def primeStr (w : List Bool) : List Bool := [decide (listToNat w).Prime]

/-- **The polynomial-time arithmetic hypothesis bundle** (plan decision "conditional
candidates", D11; inventory items Rem-33.2, Rem-43.6, Rem-48.2 and findings F1/F6):
binary multiplication, addition, truncated subtraction, division with remainder, the
extended Euclidean algorithm [PS10, Algorithm 43.2, Claim 43.3], modular exponentiation
[PS10, Algorithm 45.5, Theorem 45.6], comparison, the bit length and primality testing
[PS10, p. 33 and §2.6.5] are polynomial-time computable on binary numerals
(`Complexity.PolyTimeComputable`).

**Deviation:** [PS10] uses these algorithms freely; the campaign states each candidate
result under this explicit hypothesis instead of building the machines, adding no axiom.

Repair (run-3 audit P7-1): the fields `add`, `sub` and `size` were added — the generators,
samplers and reductions of [PS10, §2.9–§2.12] decrement (`Φ(N) = (p−1)(q−1)`), subtract
modulo `N` (`gcd(x − z, N)`, Algorithm 62.9), add (the CRT root formula, Theorem 58.3) and
read bit lengths (`k = Nat.size N` bits per rejection trial); all three are derivable from
`mul` and `divMod` in principle (`a + b = ((2^{2k} + a)(2^{2k} + b) mod 2^{4k}) / 2^{2k}`, the
bit length by a search with `le`), but that is the machine building the campaign excludes.
Every field is a true statement about a total FP function, so the bundle is satisfiable. -/
structure ArithmeticFP : Prop where
  /-- Binary multiplication is polynomial-time. -/
  mul : PolyTimeComputable mulStr
  /-- Binary addition is polynomial-time (run-3 audit P7-1). -/
  add : PolyTimeComputable addStr
  /-- Truncated binary subtraction is polynomial-time (run-3 audit P7-1). -/
  sub : PolyTimeComputable subStr
  /-- Division with remainder is polynomial-time. -/
  divMod : PolyTimeComputable divModStr
  /-- The extended Euclidean algorithm (gcd and modular inverse) is polynomial-time
  [PS10, Claim 43.3]. -/
  xgcd : PolyTimeComputable xgcdStr
  /-- Modular exponentiation is polynomial-time [PS10, Theorem 45.6]. -/
  modExp : PolyTimeComputable modExpStr
  /-- Comparison of binary numerals is polynomial-time. -/
  le : PolyTimeComputable leStr
  /-- The bit length (in unary) of a binary numeral is polynomial-time (run-3 audit P7-1). -/
  size : PolyTimeComputable sizeStr
  /-- Primality testing is polynomial-time [PS10, p. 33, AKS]. -/
  prime : PolyTimeComputable primeStr

/-! ### Unfolding lemmas -/

/-- `mulStr` on an encoded pair. -/
@[simp] theorem mulStr_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) :
    mulStr (pairEncode a b) = natToList (a.length + b.length) (listToNat a * listToNat b) := by
  simp [mulStr]

/-- `mulStr` on the numerals of `M` and `N` (widths `k` and `l`) is the `(k + l)`-bit numeral
of `M · N`. -/
theorem mulStr_natToList (k l M N : ℕ) (hM : M < 2 ^ k) (hN : N < 2 ^ l) :
    mulStr (pairEncode (natToList k M) (natToList l N)) = natToList (k + l) (M * N) := by
  rw [mulStr_pairEncode, length_natToList, length_natToList, listToNat_natToList hM,
    listToNat_natToList hN]

/-- **The product word reads back exactly**: `⟦mulStr ⟨a, b⟩⟧ = ⟦a⟧ · ⟦b⟧` (the product fits in
`|a| + |b|` bits). -/
theorem listToNat_mulStr (a b : List Bool) :
    listToNat (mulStr (pairEncode a b)) = listToNat a * listToNat b := by
  rw [mulStr_pairEncode, listToNat_natToList]
  rw [pow_add]
  exact Nat.mul_lt_mul'' (listToNat_lt_two_pow a) (listToNat_lt_two_pow b)

/-- `addStr` on an encoded pair. -/
@[simp] theorem addStr_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) :
    addStr (pairEncode a b) = natToList (a.length + b.length) (listToNat a + listToNat b) := by
  simp [addStr]

/-- `subStr` on an encoded pair. -/
@[simp] theorem subStr_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) :
    subStr (pairEncode a b) = natToList a.length (listToNat a - listToNat b) := by
  simp [subStr]

/-- The defining equation of `sizeStr`: `sizeStr w = 1^{Nat.size (listToNat w)}`, the bit length
of the number read from `w`, in unary. -/
theorem sizeStr_eq (w : List Bool) :
    sizeStr w = List.replicate (Nat.size (listToNat w)) true := rfl

/-- `sizeStr w` is the unary bit length of the number read from `w`. -/
@[simp] theorem length_sizeStr (w : List Bool) : (sizeStr w).length = Nat.size (listToNat w) := by
  simp [sizeStr]

/-- The sum of the numbers read from two numerals is below `2^{|a| + |b|}`.

**Proof sketch.** If one numeral is empty it reads as `0` and the claim is
`listToNat_lt_two_pow` of the other; otherwise `a, b ≤ 2^{|a|} − 1, 2^{|b|} − 1` and
`2^{|a|} + 2^{|b|} ≤ 2^{|a|} · 2^{|b|}` since both powers are at least `2`
(`(x − 1)(y − 1) ≥ 1`, `nlinarith`). -/
theorem listToNat_add_lt_two_pow (a b : List Bool) :
    listToNat a + listToNat b < 2 ^ (a.length + b.length) := by
  have ha := listToNat_lt_two_pow a
  have hb := listToNat_lt_two_pow b
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos a.length with h0 | hpos
  · rw [h0] at ha ⊢
    simp only [pow_zero, Nat.lt_one_iff] at ha
    rw [ha, zero_add, zero_add]
    exact hb
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos b.length with h0' | hpos'
  · rw [h0'] at hb ⊢
    simp only [pow_zero, Nat.lt_one_iff] at hb
    rw [hb, add_zero, add_zero]
    exact ha
  have h2a : 2 ≤ 2 ^ a.length := by
    calc 2 = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
      _ ≤ 2 ^ a.length := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hpos
  have h2b : 2 ≤ 2 ^ b.length := by
    calc 2 = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
      _ ≤ 2 ^ b.length := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hpos'
  rw [pow_add]
  nlinarith

/-- **Addition is lossless**: `addStr ⟨a, b⟩` reads back as `a + b`. -/
theorem listToNat_addStr (a b : List Bool) :
    listToNat (addStr (pairEncode a b)) = listToNat a + listToNat b := by
  rw [addStr_pairEncode, listToNat_natToList (listToNat_add_lt_two_pow a b)]

/-- **Truncated subtraction is lossless**: `subStr ⟨a, b⟩` reads back as `a ∸ b`. -/
theorem listToNat_subStr (a b : List Bool) :
    listToNat (subStr (pairEncode a b)) = listToNat a - listToNat b := by
  rw [subStr_pairEncode]
  exact listToNat_natToList (lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le _ _) (listToNat_lt_two_pow a))

/-- **Subtracting a word from itself** gives the zero numeral of its width:
`subStr ⟨a, a⟩ = ⟦0⟧_{|a|}`. -/
theorem subStr_self (a : List Bool) : subStr (pairEncode a a) = natToList a.length 0 := by
  rw [subStr_pairEncode, Nat.sub_self]

/-- `divModStr` on an encoded pair: `divModStr ⟨a, b⟩ = ⟨⟦a / b⟧_{|a|}, ⟦a mod b⟧_{|b|}⟩`, the
quotient as an `|a|`-bit and the remainder as a `|b|`-bit numeral (`a / 0 = 0`, `a mod 0 = a`). -/
theorem divModStr_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) :
    divModStr (pairEncode a b) = pairEncode (natToList a.length (listToNat a / listToNat b))
      (natToList b.length (listToNat a % listToNat b)) := by
  simp [divModStr]

/-- `xgcdStr` on an encoded pair: `xgcdStr ⟨a, b⟩ = ⟨⟦gcd(a, b)⟧_{|b|}, ⟦(a : Z_b)⁻¹⟧_{|b|}⟩`, the
gcd and the residue of `ZMod.inv` of `a` modulo `b`, both as `|b|`-bit numerals. -/
theorem xgcdStr_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) :
    xgcdStr (pairEncode a b) = pairEncode (natToList b.length (Nat.gcd (listToNat a) (listToNat b)))
      (natToList b.length ((listToNat a : ZMod (listToNat b))⁻¹).val) := by
  unfold xgcdStr
  rw [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]

/-- In `Z_0 = ℤ` the inverse of a natural number is its sign, so its value is at most `1`:
`((e : Z_0)⁻¹).val ≤ 1` (the `N = 0` case of `xgcdStr_pairEncode`'s inverse). -/
theorem val_inv_natCast_zmod_zero_le (e : ℕ) : ((e : ZMod 0)⁻¹).val ≤ 1 := by
  show (Int.sign (e : ℤ)).natAbs ≤ 1
  rw [Int.natAbs_sign]
  split_ifs <;> omega

/-- `leStr` on an encoded pair. -/
@[simp] theorem leStr_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) :
    leStr (pairEncode a b) = [decide (listToNat a ≤ listToNat b)] := by
  simp [leStr]

/-- `modExpStr` on an encoded triple. -/
@[simp] theorem modExpStr_pairEncode (a x N : List Bool) :
    modExpStr (pairEncode a (pairEncode x N)) =
      natToList N.length (listToNat a ^ listToNat x % listToNat N) := by
  simp [modExpStr]

/-- `primeStr` is the primality test of `exists_samplePrime_nuppt`. -/
theorem primeStr_eq : primeStr = fun w : List Bool => [decide (listToNat w).Prime] := rfl

/-- **Comparisons are polynomial-time tests**: for polynomial-time words `a`, `b`, the bit
`[⟦a x⟧ ≤ ⟦b x⟧]` is polynomial-time (`H.le`, read through `leStr_pairEncode`). -/
theorem ArithmeticFP.le_poly (H : ArithmeticFP) {a b : List Bool → List Bool}
    (ha : PolyTimeComputable a) (hb : PolyTimeComputable b) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x => [decide (listToNat (a x) ≤ listToNat (b x))] :=
  (PolyTimeComputable.comp' H.le (ha.pairEncode hb)).congr fun x => leStr_pairEncode (a x) (b x)

/-- **Primality of a polynomial-time word is a polynomial-time test**: for a polynomial-time
word `a`, the bit `[⟦a x⟧ is prime]` is polynomial-time (`H.prime`, `primeStr_eq`). -/
theorem ArithmeticFP.prime_poly (H : ArithmeticFP) {a : List Bool → List Bool}
    (ha : PolyTimeComputable a) : PolyTimeComputable fun x => [decide (listToNat (a x)).Prime] :=
  (PolyTimeComputable.comp' H.prime ha).congr fun x => congrFun primeStr_eq (a x)

/-- The residue of `x^e` is `x.val^e mod M` for a unit `x` of `Z_M` (any modulus `M ≠ 0`): the
form in which the evaluators `modExpStr` compute the permutations `x ↦ x^e` and `x ↦ x²`
(moved from `RSA.lean`, run-3 audit P7-6). -/
theorem val_units_pow (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (x : (ZMod M)ˣ) (e : ℕ) :
    ((x ^ e : (ZMod M)ˣ) : ZMod M).val = (x : ZMod M).val ^ e % M := by
  rw [Units.val_pow_eq_pow_val, ← ZMod.val_natCast, Nat.cast_pow, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]

/-- The product of two `k`-bit numbers is below `2^(k + k)`. -/
theorem mul_lt_two_pow_add {k M N : ℕ} (hM : M < 2 ^ k) (hN : N < 2 ^ k) : M * N < 2 ^ (k + k) := by
  rw [pow_add]
  exact Nat.mul_lt_mul'' hM hN

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates
```

```text
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.Modular
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.ModularDecode
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.BinaryArith
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.DyadicArithmetic
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.DyadicUniform
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.DyadicLinearAlgebra
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.BooleanVector

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary encodings for cryptographic problem instances

## Contents

* `Modular`: fixed-width modular vector and row-major matrix encodings, their
  defining equations, and their proved length/injectivity guarantees.
* `ModularDecode`: canonical parsers, rejection equations and statement-phase round trips.
* `BinaryArith`: endian and polynomial-width adapter statements for existing binary machines.
* `DyadicArithmetic`: scalar modular addition, multiplication and subtraction statements.
* `DyadicUniform`: exact fair-bit residue, vector and matrix sampling laws.
* `DyadicLinearAlgebra`: counted-loop encoded dot products and matrix-vector multiplication.
* `BooleanVector`: false-padded binary domain words as encoded modular vectors.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, author version dated
  17 February 2016, Definitions 4.1.1 and 4.2.3.
-/
```


## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Encoding/BinaryArith.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Arithmetic
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.EnsemblesLemmas
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Mul
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Primitives

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary arithmetic representation adapters

## Main definitions

* `toLE`: reverse a most-significant-bit-first word and normalize the result.
* `normalizeWidthPoly`: pad or truncate an MSB word to a polynomial parameter width.
* `fromLEPoly`: write a little-endian word in the canonical fixed-width MSB format.

## Main results

The semantic equations, exact output widths, normalization and round-trip formulas,
and all three polynomial-time contracts are proved. They handle arbitrary parameter
templates, malformed pairs and zero widths. Complete cryptographic implementations
and primitive-security theorems remain separate consumer obligations.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed.,
  January 2010, Section 2.1 (bit-string machine representations).
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009, Section 7.2 (the surrounding machine model).

**Representation adaptation.** These are technical repository adapters, rather than
textbook arithmetic theorems. Candidates uses fixed-width MSB words; the existing
`Complexity.BinArith` machines use normalized little-endian `Nat.bits` words. Reuse
`BinaryArith.Basic` and `BinaryArith.Mul` for normalization/reversal, the polynomial
cut contracts in `Randomized.Primitives`, and `EnsembleLemmas.polyTimeComputable_zeros`.
No private padding, traversal or arithmetic host is introduced. Their full axiom
dependencies still require the consumer gate; a filled source body alone is not
that certificate.

Parameter templates are arbitrary words: only their lengths matter. Pair projections
are total, so malformed pairs give the width at parameter zero and an empty payload.
Zero widths are allowed. Width normalization keeps the low bits, which differs from
the existing right-padding/prefix convention. No numeric fit premise is needed until
claiming a lossless round trip.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.BinaryArith

open Complexity Turing
open TCSlib.Cryptography.NumberTheory (listToNat)

/-- Convert an MSB word to normalized little-endian bits by reversing and normalizing
it [PS10, Section 2.1, repository representation adaptation]. -/
def toLE (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  Nat.bits (LogProg.bitsVal w.reverse)

/-- `toLE w` is `Nat.bits (LogProg.bitsVal w.reverse)`. -/
theorem toLE_eq (w : List Bool) :
    toLE w = Nat.bits (LogProg.bitsVal w.reverse) := rfl

/-- Conversion produces the normalized little-endian numeral of the MSB word's value.

**Proof sketch.** Prove the endian equality locally by induction on the word using
`NumberTheory.listToNat_nil`, `listToNat_cons`, list reversal equations and
`BinArith.bitsVal_append_singleton`. Apply `Nat.bits` to that equality. -/
theorem toLE_eq_natBits (w : List Bool) :
    toLE w = Nat.bits (listToNat w) := by
  rw [toLE_eq]
  apply congrArg Nat.bits
  induction w with
  | nil =>
      rw [List.reverse_nil, NumberTheory.listToNat_nil]
      exact (BinArith.bitsVal_eq_zero_iff []).2 rfl
  | cons b w ih =>
      rw [List.reverse_cons, BinArith.bitsVal_append_singleton,
        List.length_reverse, ih, NumberTheory.listToNat_cons]
      cases b with
      | false =>
          simp only [Bool.toNat_false, if_neg Bool.false_ne_true,
            Nat.zero_mul, Nat.add_zero, Nat.zero_add]
      | true =>
          simp only [Bool.toNat_true, if_true, Nat.one_mul]
          exact Nat.add_comm _ _

/-- Reading the converted little-endian word recovers the original MSB value.

**Proof sketch.** Use `toLE_eq_natBits` and the existing `LogProg.bitsVal_bits` equation. -/
theorem bitsVal_toLE (w : List Bool) :
    LogProg.bitsVal (toLE w) = listToNat w := by
  rw [toLE_eq_natBits, LogProg.bitsVal_bits]

/-- Converting to a normalized little-endian word never increases its length.

**Proof sketch.** Read `toLE_eq`, apply `BinArith.length_bits_bitsVal_le` to the reversed
word, and use the length equation for reversal. This includes empty and all-zero words. -/
theorem length_toLE_le (w : List Bool) :
    (toLE w).length ≤ w.length := by
  rw [toLE_eq]
  simpa only [List.length_reverse] using
    BinArith.length_bits_bitsVal_le w.reverse

/-- Conversion from MSB to normalized little-endian words is polynomial-time.
This is technical representation infrastructure for the existing machine model.

**Proof sketch.** Compose `BinArith.polyTimeComputable_reverse` with
`BinArith.polyTimeComputable_normBits`; read the normalizer's public contract and
`toLE_eq`. No new machine or host is required. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_toLE : PolyTimeComputable toLE := by
  have h : PolyTimeComputable
      (fun w => Nat.bits (LogProg.bitsVal w.reverse)) :=
    BinArith.polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp
      BinArith.polyTimeComputable_reverse
  have heq : toLE = (fun w => Nat.bits (LogProg.bitsVal w.reverse)) :=
    funext toLE_eq
  exact heq.symm ▸ h

/-- Normalize the second pair component to `p` evaluated at the first component's
length, by prepending zeros and retaining the low bits
[PS10, Section 2.1, explicit polynomial-width adaptation]. -/
def normalizeWidthPoly (p : PolyExpr) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (List.replicate (p.eval (pairFstD z).length) false ++ pairSndD z).drop
    (pairSndD z).length

/-- Width normalization prepends the requested number of zeros and drops as many
bits as the original second component has. -/
theorem normalizeWidthPoly_eq (p : PolyExpr) (z : List Bool) :
    normalizeWidthPoly p z =
      (List.replicate (p.eval (pairFstD z).length) false ++ pairSndD z).drop
        (pairSndD z).length := rfl

/-- On an encoded pair, width normalization writes the second word's value at the
width `p.eval u.length`, truncating only high bits when necessary.

**Proof sketch.** Read the pair projections and `normalizeWidthPoly_eq`. Identify an
all-zero word with the zero numeral using the existing numeral round trip and
`Candidates.listToNat_replicate_false`. Apply `Candidates.natToList_zero_append_drop`.
This works for arbitrary payload and target lengths, including zero. -/
theorem normalizeWidthPoly_pairEncode (p : PolyExpr) (u w : List Bool) :
    normalizeWidthPoly p (pairEncode u w) =
      Candidates.natToList (p.eval u.length) (listToNat w) := by
  have hzero :
      Candidates.natToList (p.eval u.length) 0 =
        List.replicate (p.eval u.length) false := by
    simpa only [List.length_replicate, Candidates.listToNat_replicate_false] using
      Candidates.natToList_length_listToNat
        (List.replicate (p.eval u.length) false)
  rw [normalizeWidthPoly_eq, pairFstD_pairEncode,
    pairSndD_pairEncode, ← hzero]
  exact Candidates.natToList_zero_append_drop (p.eval u.length) w

/-- The normalized word has exactly the requested polynomial width on every input.

**Proof sketch.** Read `normalizeWidthPoly_eq` and the public append, replicate and
drop length equations. Natural arithmetic cancels the payload length; no valid-pair
premise or positive-width premise is needed. -/
```
