```text
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE.Basic
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE.Bits
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE.Flat

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Direct generators from decisional LWE

## Contents

* `Basic`: the structured generator, DLWE pseudorandomness and exact entropy budgets.
* `Bits`: the MSB encoded generator on explicit independent seed blocks.
* `Flat`: a single-word generator built from existing little-endian finite bit equivalences.

All nontrivial new statements are admitted for the combined statement audit.
The child modules distinguish actual laws and deterministic mathematics from
efficiency/security endpoints. Source-policy work and user-controlled integration
remain open; this facade claims no completed primitive or CCA2 security.
-/
```


## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Pseudorandom/Generators/LWE/Basic.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.Assumption
import TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.BitNoise
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators

import Mathlib.Tactic.Simps.Basic

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The direct DLWE generator and its entropy budget

## Main definitions

* `generate`: publish the existing `(A, As+e)` sample with the matrix included in the seed.
* `seedBitLength`, `outputBitLength`: exact dyadic bit counts, including all noise seeds.

## Main results

The concrete generator advantage equals the existing DLWE advantage. The fixed-sample
assumption implies pseudorandomness against the existing encoded machine tests.
Cardinality and stretch statements expose the additional entropy requirement.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, 17 February 2016,
  Definition 4.2.3 (the pseudorandom LWE sample distribution).
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, 22 January 2026,
  Definition 3.5 (generator distinguishing advantage).

Viewing the DLWE sample map as a generator is a repository adaptation of these
definitions. Seed compression requires the displayed strict entropy inequality;
it does not follow from DLWE alone for an arbitrary finite-noise sampler.
The existing asymptotic PRG type indexes by its exact seed length. These statements
do not hide the separate reindexing, finite-small-length and efficient implementation
obligations needed to construct that type. No PRF-based construction is used.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE

open Complexity (NUPPT)
open TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE (Parameters Noise Family)

/-- Publish the matrix and its noisy common-secret product, using exactly the existing
LWE sampler [Pei16, Definition 4.2.3; Gar26, Definition 3.5, adaptation]. -/
@[simps! (config := { isSimp := false }) fst snd]
def generate (P : Parameters) (χ : Noise)
    (r : Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
      ((Fin P.dimension → ZMod P.modulus) × (Fin P.samples → χ.Coins))) :
    Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
      (Fin P.samples → ZMod P.modulus) :=
  TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.sample P χ r

/-- The complete generator map is the original finite-sample LWE map. -/
theorem generate_eq (P : Parameters) (χ : Noise)
    (r : Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
      ((Fin P.dimension → ZMod P.modulus) × (Fin P.samples → χ.Coins))) :
    generate P χ r = TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.sample P χ r := rfl

/-- The generator's concrete advantage is exactly the decisional LWE advantage
[Pei16, Definition 4.2.3; Gar26, Definition 3.5].

**Proof sketch.** Read the public generator and advantage equations. Both experiments
use the same real sampler and the identity on the full independent uniform output. -/
theorem prgAdv_generate {ρ : Type*} [Fintype ρ] [Nonempty ρ]
    (P : Parameters) (χ : Noise)
    (D : (Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
      (Fin P.samples → ZMod P.modulus)) → ρ → Bool) :
    prgAdv (generate P χ) D = TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.decisionAdvantage P χ D := by
  have hg : generate P χ = TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.sample P χ :=
    funext (generate_eq P χ)
  rw [prgAdv_eq, TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.decisionAdvantage_eq, hg]

/-- The fixed-sample DLWE assumption supplies negligible generator advantage for
every existing encoded non-uniform PPT test [Pei16, Definition 4.2.3].

**Proof sketch.** Apply the assumption's public characterization to the same machine,
then rewrite each pointwise advantage with `prgAdv_generate` and `Family.advantageAt_eq`.
This transfers pseudorandomness only; no efficient generator or stretch claim is inferred. -/
theorem pseudorandom_under_DLWE (F : Family)
    (h : TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.DLWEAssumption F) (D : NUPPT) :
    Negligible (fun κ => prgAdv (generate (F.parameters κ) (F.noise κ))
      (fun x r => D.distinguisherL κ
        (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge (F.parameters κ)
          (F.residueBits.eval κ) x) r)) := by
  have hD := (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.dlweAssumption_iff F).mp h D
  simpa only [prgAdv_generate, TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.Family.advantageAt_eq] using hD

/-- Count the seed bits for the full matrix, one secret, and `t` independent noise
bits per row [Pei16, Definition 4.2.3, explicit entropy accounting]. -/
def seedBitLength (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  P.samples * P.dimension * width + P.dimension * width + P.samples * t

/-- The seed budget includes matrix, secret and all scalar-noise seed blocks. -/
theorem seedBitLength_eq (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) :
    seedBitLength P width t =
      P.samples * P.dimension * width + P.dimension * width + P.samples * t := rfl

/-- Count the published matrix-and-value bits in the existing challenge encoding. -/
def outputBitLength (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  P.samples * (P.dimension + 1) * width

/-- The output budget is the full matrix plus one residue value per sample. -/
theorem outputBitLength_eq (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ) :
    outputBitLength P width = P.samples * (P.dimension + 1) * width := rfl

/-- For dyadic residues and explicit `t`-bit noise, the real seed space has exactly
`2^seedBitLength` elements [Pei16, Definition 4.2.3, bit-seed specialization].

**Proof sketch.** Evaluate the finite matrix, vector, Boolean function and product
cardinalities. Substitute `q=2^width` and combine the powers using their natural exponents. -/
theorem seed_cardinality (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ)
    (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) (f : (Fin t → Bool) → ℤ) :
    Fintype.card (Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
      ((Fin P.dimension → ZMod P.modulus) ×
        (Fin P.samples → (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise t f).Coins))) =
      2 ^ seedBitLength P width t := by
  change Fintype.card ((Fin P.samples → Fin P.dimension → ZMod P.modulus) ×
    ((Fin P.dimension → ZMod P.modulus) ×
      (Fin P.samples → (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise t f).Coins))) = _
  rw [seedBitLength_eq]
  simp only [TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise_Coins, Fintype.card_prod,
    Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool, ZMod.card, hq]
  simp only [← pow_mul, ← pow_add]
  congr 1
  ac_rfl

/-- The full dyadic output space has exactly `2^outputBitLength` elements.

**Proof sketch.** Evaluate the matrix and value-vector cardinalities, substitute
the exact power-of-two modulus, and distribute the natural exponent products. -/
theorem output_cardinality (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ)
    (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    Fintype.card (Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
      (Fin P.samples → ZMod P.modulus)) = 2 ^ outputBitLength P width := by
  change Fintype.card ((Fin P.samples → Fin P.dimension → ZMod P.modulus) ×
    (Fin P.samples → ZMod P.modulus)) = _
  rw [outputBitLength_eq]
  simp only [Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin, ZMod.card, hq]
  simp only [← pow_mul, ← pow_add]
  congr 1
  simp only [Nat.mul_add, Nat.add_mul, Nat.mul_one]
  ac_rfl

/-- Positive stretch is equivalent to paying for the secret and noise from the
published value-vector budget. The matrix is counted on both sides.

**Proof sketch.** Expand both bit counts, distribute the output's multiplication,
and cancel the common nonnegative matrix budget from the strict inequality. -/
theorem stretch_iff (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) :
    seedBitLength P width t < outputBitLength P width ↔
      P.dimension * width + P.samples * t < P.samples * width := by
  rw [seedBitLength_eq, outputBitLength_eq]
  simp only [Nat.mul_add, Nat.add_mul, Nat.mul_one,
    Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_lt_add_iff_left]

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE
```


## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Pseudorandom/Generators/LWE/Bits.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE.Basic
import TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.Sampling

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The DLWE generator on explicit bit blocks

## Main definitions

* `generateBits`: sample from explicit fair-bit blocks and publish the canonical encoding.

## Main results

The output has its exact claimed length and its advantage against a full uniform
output word equals the DLWE advantage of the encoded test. The input cardinality
records every consumed bit. These representation and advantage identities are proved below.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, 17 February 2016,
  Definition 4.2.3.
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, 22 January 2026,
  Definition 3.5.

These structured input blocks are in bijection with words of `seedBitLength` bits.
No efficient flattening/reindexing machine or instance of the existing exact-seed-indexed
asymptotic PRG structure is claimed here. In particular a noise seed's full bit cost
cannot be replaced by the logarithm of its support size without a new sampler proof.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE

open TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE (Parameters)

/-- Encode the actual explicit-bit LWE sample as the generator output
[Pei16, Definition 4.2.3; Gar26, Definition 3.5, representation adaptation]. -/
def generateBits (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) (f : (Fin t → Bool) → ℤ)
    (r : (Fin P.samples → Fin P.dimension → Fin width → Bool) ×
      ((Fin P.dimension → Fin width → Bool) × (Fin P.samples → Fin t → Bool))) : List Bool :=
  TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width
    (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.sampleFromBits P width t f r)

/-- The bit generator applies exactly the public challenge encoding to its bit sampler. -/
theorem generateBits_eq (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) (f : (Fin t → Bool) → ℤ)
    (r : (Fin P.samples → Fin P.dimension → Fin width → Bool) ×
      ((Fin P.dimension → Fin width → Bool) × (Fin P.samples → Fin t → Bool))) :
    generateBits P width t f r = TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width
      (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.sampleFromBits P width t f r) := rfl

/-- Every output has exactly the full matrix-and-value bit length, without a modulus
coverage premise.

**Proof sketch.** Read `generateBits_eq` and the existing `encodeChallenge_length`.
The length is fixed even at a width too small to be faithful. -/
theorem generateBits_length (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ)
    (f : (Fin t → Bool) → ℤ)
    (r : (Fin P.samples → Fin P.dimension → Fin width → Bool) ×
      ((Fin P.dimension → Fin width → Bool) × (Fin P.samples → Fin t → Bool))) :
    (generateBits P width t f r).length = outputBitLength P width := by
  rw [generateBits_eq, TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge_length, outputBitLength_eq]

/-- The structured fair-bit seed contains exactly the declared number of independent
bits, including all scalar-noise seeds.

**Proof sketch.** Count finite functions and products, then combine powers of two.
No modulus premise is needed because every input factor is already a bit type. -/
theorem bit_seed_cardinality (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card ((Fin P.samples → Fin P.dimension → Fin width → Bool) ×
      ((Fin P.dimension → Fin width → Bool) × (Fin P.samples → Fin t → Bool))) =
      2 ^ seedBitLength P width t := by
  rw [seedBitLength_eq]
  simp only [Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool]
  simp only [← pow_mul, ← pow_add]
  congr 1
  ac_rfl

/-- Against a full uniform output word, the explicit bit generator has exactly the
DLWE advantage of the canonically encoded test [Pei16, Definition 4.2.3].

**Proof sketch.** The real side is `acceptProb_sampleFromBits` with encoding composed
into the test. At a dyadic modulus, encoding is a bijection onto all words of the
declared output length: combine the existing faithful challenge encoder's injectivity
with the proved output cardinality, using the concrete word reader. Relabel the ideal
uniform word by that bijection, preserving all test coins. -/
theorem generateBits_advantage {ρ : Type*} [Fintype ρ] [Nonempty ρ]
    (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width)
    (f : (Fin t → Bool) → ℤ) (D : List Bool → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv (generateBits P width t f)
      (fun u : Fin (outputBitLength P width) → Bool => List.ofFn u) D =
      TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.decisionAdvantage P
        (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise t f)
        (fun x r => D (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x) r) := by
  classical
  let X := Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
    (Fin P.samples → ZMod P.modulus)
  let L := outputBitLength P width
  have hlen (x : X) : (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x).length = L := by
    change (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x).length = outputBitLength P width
    rw [TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge_length, outputBitLength_eq]
  let enc : X → Fin L → Bool := fun x i =>
    (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x).get
      (Fin.cast (hlen x).symm i)
  have henc (x : X) : List.ofFn (enc x) =
      TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x := by
    exact (List.ofFn_congr (hlen x)
      (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x).get).symm.trans
        (List.ofFn_get _)
  have hinj : Function.Injective enc := by
    intro x y hxy
    apply TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge_injective P width hq.le
    calc
      TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x = List.ofFn (enc x) := (henc x).symm
      _ = List.ofFn (enc y) := congrArg List.ofFn hxy
      _ = TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width y := henc y
  have hcard : Fintype.card X = Fintype.card (Fin L → Bool) := by
    simpa only [Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool]
      using output_cardinality P width hq
  let e : X ≃ (Fin L → Bool) := Equiv.ofBijective enc
    ((Fintype.bijective_iff_injective_and_card enc).mpr ⟨hinj, hcard⟩)
  have he (x : X) : List.ofFn (e x) =
      TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x := henc x
  have hreal : acceptProb (generateBits P width t f) D =
      acceptProb (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.sample P (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise t f))
        (fun x r => D (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x) r) := by
    simpa only [acceptProb_def, generateBits_eq] using
      (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.acceptProb_sampleFromBits P width t hq f
        (fun x r => D (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x) r))
  have hideal : acceptProb (fun u : Fin L → Bool => List.ofFn u) D =
      acceptProb (id : X → X)
        (fun x r => D (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.encodeChallenge P width x) r) := by
    rw [← acceptProb_comp_equiv e (fun u : Fin L → Bool => List.ofFn u) D]
    simp only [acceptProb_def, he, id_eq]
  simp only [TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.decisionAdvantage_eq, distAdv_def, hreal]
  rw [hideal]

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE
```


## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Pseudorandom/Generators/LWE/Flat.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE.Basic
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.RandomBits

import Mathlib.Tactic.Simps.Basic

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# A single-word direct DLWE generator

## Main definitions

* `vectorBitsEquiv`, `matrixBitsEquiv`, `noiseBitsEquiv`: explicit existing bit-block packings.
* `flatSeedEquiv`, `flatOutputEquiv`: combine the independent seed and output components.
* `generateFlat`: run the original DLWE sampler between those two bit equivalences.

## Main results

The generator accepts one word of exactly the full seed budget and outputs one word
of exactly the matrix-and-value budget. Its advantage equals the actual DLWE advantage
of the explicitly re-encoded test. These identities are proved below.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, 17 February 2016,
  Definition 4.2.3.
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, 22 January 2026,
  Definition 3.5.

The concrete map uses the existing little-endian finite bit equivalences, not an
arbitrary cardinality-choice bijection. The sibling `Bits` module uses the existing
MSB challenge codec; both conventions are explicit. A uniform parameter schedule,
efficient noise implementation, and the conversion from this parameterization to the
existing exact-seed-indexed asymptotic PRG remain separate obligations.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE

open TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE (Parameters)

/-- Pack `length` full-width bit blocks as a residue vector at a dyadic modulus. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) apply symm_apply]
def vectorBitsEquiv (P : Parameters) (width length : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    (Fin (length * width) → Bool) ≃ (Fin length → ZMod P.modulus) :=
  (Randomized.blocksEquiv length width).trans
    (Equiv.arrowCongr (Equiv.refl (Fin length))
      ((finCongr hq.symm).trans (ZMod.finEquiv P.modulus).toEquiv))

/-- The complete vector packing composes block packing, the modulus cast and `ZMod.finEquiv`. -/
theorem vectorBitsEquiv_eq (P : Parameters) (width length : ℕ)
    (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    vectorBitsEquiv P width length hq =
      (Randomized.blocksEquiv length width).trans
        (Equiv.arrowCongr (Equiv.refl (Fin length))
          ((finCongr hq.symm).trans (ZMod.finEquiv P.modulus).toEquiv)) := rfl

/-- Pack the matrix portion row by row using existing product-index and curry equivalences. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) apply symm_apply]
def matrixBitsEquiv (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    (Fin (P.samples * P.dimension * width) → Bool) ≃
      Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) :=
  (vectorBitsEquiv P width (P.samples * P.dimension) hq).trans
    ((Equiv.arrowCongr finProdFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl (ZMod P.modulus))).trans
      (Equiv.curry (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus)))

/-- The complete matrix packing first reads residues, then restores their row/column indices. -/
theorem matrixBitsEquiv_eq (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    matrixBitsEquiv P width hq =
      (vectorBitsEquiv P width (P.samples * P.dimension) hq).trans
        ((Equiv.arrowCongr finProdFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl (ZMod P.modulus))).trans
          (Equiv.curry (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus))) := rfl

/-- Partition one noise word into exactly one independent `t`-bit seed per LWE row. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) apply symm_apply]
def noiseBitsEquiv (m t : ℕ) :
    (Fin (m * t) → Bool) ≃ (Fin m → Fin t → Bool) :=
  (Equiv.arrowCongr finProdFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl Bool)).trans
    (Equiv.curry (Fin m) (Fin t) Bool)

/-- The complete noise packing only regroups existing bits; it does not resample errors. -/
theorem noiseBitsEquiv_eq (m t : ℕ) :
    noiseBitsEquiv m t =
      (Equiv.arrowCongr finProdFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl Bool)).trans
        (Equiv.curry (Fin m) (Fin t) Bool) := rfl

/-- Split one flat seed into the matrix, common secret and all original noise seeds
[Pei16, Definition 4.2.3, explicit bit packing]. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) apply symm_apply]
def flatSeedEquiv (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    (Fin (P.samples * P.dimension * width + (P.dimension * width + P.samples * t)) → Bool) ≃
      (Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
        ((Fin P.dimension → ZMod P.modulus) × (Fin P.samples → Fin t → Bool))) :=
  (Fin.appendEquiv (P.samples * P.dimension * width)
    (P.dimension * width + P.samples * t)).symm.trans
    ((matrixBitsEquiv P width hq).prodCongr
      ((Fin.appendEquiv (P.dimension * width) (P.samples * t)).symm.trans
        ((vectorBitsEquiv P width P.dimension hq).prodCongr
          (noiseBitsEquiv P.samples t))))

/-- The complete flat seed equivalence splits the three budgets and applies their packings. -/
theorem flatSeedEquiv_eq (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    flatSeedEquiv P width t hq =
      (Fin.appendEquiv (P.samples * P.dimension * width)
        (P.dimension * width + P.samples * t)).symm.trans
        ((matrixBitsEquiv P width hq).prodCongr
          ((Fin.appendEquiv (P.dimension * width) (P.samples * t)).symm.trans
            ((vectorBitsEquiv P width P.dimension hq).prodCongr
              (noiseBitsEquiv P.samples t)))) := rfl

/-- Pack a flat output word as the full matrix followed by an independent value vector. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) apply symm_apply]
def flatOutputEquiv (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    (Fin (P.samples * P.dimension * width + P.samples * width) → Bool) ≃
      (Matrix (Fin P.samples) (Fin P.dimension) (ZMod P.modulus) ×
        (Fin P.samples → ZMod P.modulus)) :=
  (Fin.appendEquiv (P.samples * P.dimension * width) (P.samples * width)).symm.trans
    ((matrixBitsEquiv P width hq).prodCongr (vectorBitsEquiv P width P.samples hq))

/-- The complete output equivalence independently packs its matrix and value-vector parts. -/
theorem flatOutputEquiv_eq (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width) :
    flatOutputEquiv P width hq =
      (Fin.appendEquiv (P.samples * P.dimension * width) (P.samples * width)).symm.trans
        ((matrixBitsEquiv P width hq).prodCongr (vectorBitsEquiv P width P.samples hq)) := rfl

/-- Generate one flat binary output by unpacking a uniform seed, applying the existing
actual-law DLWE sampler, and repacking its output [Pei16, Definition 4.2.3]. -/
def generateFlat (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width)
    (f : (Fin t → Bool) → ℤ)
    (r : Fin (P.samples * P.dimension * width + (P.dimension * width + P.samples * t)) → Bool) :
    Fin (P.samples * P.dimension * width + P.samples * width) → Bool :=
  (flatOutputEquiv P width hq).symm
    (generate P (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise t f) (flatSeedEquiv P width t hq r))

/-- The complete generator applies exactly the specified unpacking, sampler and repacking. -/
theorem generateFlat_eq (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width)
    (f : (Fin t → Bool) → ℤ)
    (r : Fin (P.samples * P.dimension * width + (P.dimension * width + P.samples * t)) → Bool) :
    generateFlat P width t hq f r = (flatOutputEquiv P width hq).symm
      (generate P (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise t f) (flatSeedEquiv P width t hq r)) := rfl

/-- Flat generator advantage equals the actual DLWE advantage of the repacked test.

**Proof sketch.** Relabel real seeds with `flatSeedEquiv` and independent uniform
outputs with `flatOutputEquiv`, keeping all distinguisher coins. Then apply the
existing `prgAdv_generate` identity. No property of the noise images is assumed. -/
theorem generateFlat_advantage {ρ : Type*} [Fintype ρ] [Nonempty ρ]
    (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) (hq : P.modulus = 2 ^ width)
    (f : (Fin t → Bool) → ℤ)
    (D : (Fin (P.samples * P.dimension * width + P.samples * width) → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    prgAdv (generateFlat P width t hq f) D =
      TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.decisionAdvantage P (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise t f)
        (fun pk r => D ((flatOutputEquiv P width hq).symm pk) r) := by
  have hG : generateFlat P width t hq f = fun r =>
      (flatOutputEquiv P width hq).symm
        (generate P (TCSlib.Cryptography.LWE.bitNoise t f)
          (flatSeedEquiv P width t hq r)) :=
    funext (generateFlat_eq P width t hq f)
  rw [hG, prgAdv_comp_equiv, ← prgAdv_generate]
  simp only [prgAdv_eq, distAdv_def]
  rw [acceptProb_comp_equiv (flatSeedEquiv P width t hq)]

/-- The flat seed type uses exactly the earlier full seed budget.

**Proof sketch.** Read `seedBitLength_eq` and reassociate natural addition. -/
theorem flat_seed_length (P : Parameters) (width t : ℕ) :
    P.samples * P.dimension * width + (P.dimension * width + P.samples * t) =
      seedBitLength P width t := by
  rw [seedBitLength_eq, Nat.add_assoc]

/-- The flat output type uses exactly the earlier full matrix-and-value budget.

**Proof sketch.** Read `outputBitLength_eq` and distribute natural multiplication. -/
theorem flat_output_length (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ) :
    P.samples * P.dimension * width + P.samples * width = outputBitLength P width := by
  rw [outputBitLength_eq]
  simp only [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one, Nat.add_mul]

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators.LWE
```


## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Pseudorandom/Indistinguishability.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Experiments

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Computational indistinguishability: the sunglass and multicopy lemmas

The concrete layer of [Gar26, §3.2]. Distributions are samplers `X : σ → γ` from uniform
seeds, distinguishers are functions `D : γ → ρ → Bool` of a sample and uniform coins, and
`distAdv X Y D` is the advantage `|Pr[D(X) = 1] - Pr[D(Y) = 1]|`. Each lemma of the source
is stated as an explicit reduction: from a distinguisher `D` for the derived pair we build a
distinguisher for `X` and `Y` and prove an exact relation between the advantages. The
asymptotic statements ("if `X ≈ Y` then ...") follow once the reductions are shown to be
efficient, which is the job of the asymptotic layer.

Besides the two lemmas, the file provides the reseeding toolkit used by all reductions in
the pseudorandomness development: invariance of acceptance probabilities under bijections
of the seed space, under unused seed coordinates, and under moving a reduction's private
coins into the sampler; plus the *index-mixing* distinguisher that picks a hybrid index
uniformly at random, which turns the hybrid argument into a uniform reduction.

## Main definitions

* `pushSampler P X`: the sampler of `P(X)` for a randomized post-processing map `P`.
* `sunglassRed P D`: the distinguisher `D ∘ P` for `X` and `Y`.
* `mixDist D`: run `D k` for a uniformly random index `k`.
* `copies t X`: `t` independent copies of `X`.
* `multicopyHybrid X Y t k`: the hybrid `(Y, …, Y, X, …, X)` with `k` copies of `Y`.
* `multicopyRed X Y t k D`: the hybrid-`k` distinguisher for one copy.
* `multicopyAvgRed X Y t D`: the same with a uniformly random `k`.

## Main results

* `uprob_eq_of_equiv`, `acceptProb_fst`, `acceptProb_snd`,
  `acceptProb_bind`, `acceptProb_update`: reseeding.
* `distAdv_mixDist_eq`: the averaged hybrid argument.
* `distAdv_sunglassRed`: [Gar26, Lemma 3.2], with equal advantage.
* `exists_multicopyRed_ge`: [Gar26, Lemma 3.3], some `k` has advantage `≥ ε / t`.
* `distAdv_multicopyAvgRed`: the averaged reduction has advantage exactly `ε / t`.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.2 (Definition 3.4, Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Finset

variable {σ τ κ ρ ι γ δ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ] [Fintype κ] [Fintype ρ]

/-! ### Reseeding -/

/-- Two events that correspond under a bijection of the sample spaces have the same
probability: if `p a` holds exactly when `q (e a)` does, then `Pr[p] = Pr[q]`. -/
theorem uprob_eq_of_equiv {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] (e : α ≃ β)
    {p : α → Prop} {q : β → Prop} (h : ∀ a, p a ↔ q (e a)) : uprob p = uprob q := by
  rw [← uprob_comp_equiv e q]
  congr 1
  funext a
  exact propext (h a)

/-- A seed coordinate that the sampler ignores does not change acceptance probabilities:
sampling `X` from the first coordinate of a uniform pair is sampling `X`. -/
theorem acceptProb_fst [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (fun z : σ × τ => X z.1) D = acceptProb X D := by
  let e : (σ × τ) × ρ ≃ (σ × ρ) × τ :=
    { toFun := fun w => ((w.1.1, w.2), w.1.2), invFun := fun z => ((z.1.1, z.2), z.1.2),
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl, right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  unfold acceptProb
  exact (uprob_eq_of_equiv e (q := fun w : (σ × ρ) × τ => D (X w.1.1) w.1.2 = true)
    fun _ => Iff.rfl).trans (uprob_fst (fun y : σ × ρ => D (X y.1) y.2 = true))

/-- As `acceptProb_fst`, for an ignored first seed coordinate. -/
theorem acceptProb_snd [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (fun z : τ × σ => X z.2) D = acceptProb X D :=
  (acceptProb_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm τ σ) (fun z : σ × τ => X z.1) D).trans
    (acceptProb_fst X D)

/-- Moving coins into the sampler: a distinguisher that first draws private coins `c` and
feeds `P z c` to `D` accepts a sample of `X` with the probability that `D` accepts a sample
of the composite sampler `(s, c) ↦ P (X s) c`. -/
theorem acceptProb_bind (X : σ → γ) (P : γ → κ → δ) (D : δ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb X (fun z (c : κ × ρ) => D (P z c.1) c.2) =
      acceptProb (fun s : σ × κ => P (X s.1) s.2) D :=
  uprob_eq_of_equiv (Equiv.prodAssoc σ κ ρ).symm fun _ => Iff.rfl

/-- Overwriting one coordinate of a uniform tuple with an independent uniform value leaves
the tuple uniform: a sampler fed `update u k x` for uniform `x` and `u` accepts with the
same probability as one fed `u`.

**Proof sketch.** The map `(x, u) ↦ (update u k x, u k)` is a bijection, and the sampler
ignores the second component of its image. -/
theorem acceptProb_update [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] [Nonempty σ] (k : ι)
    (Z : (ι → σ) → τ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (fun w : σ × ((ι → σ) × τ) => Z (Function.update w.2.1 k w.1) w.2.2) D =
      acceptProb (fun v : (ι → σ) × τ => Z v.1 v.2) D := by
  let e : σ × ((ι → σ) × τ) ≃ ((ι → σ) × τ) × σ :=
    { toFun := fun w => ((Function.update w.2.1 k w.1, w.2.2), w.2.1 k)
      invFun := fun v => (v.1.1 k, (Function.update v.1.1 k v.2, v.1.2))
      left_inv := fun w => by ext <;> simp
      right_inv := fun v => by ext <;> simp }
  rw [← acceptProb_fst (τ := σ) (fun v : (ι → σ) × τ => Z v.1 v.2) D]
  exact acceptProb_comp_equiv e (fun w : ((ι → σ) × τ) × σ => Z w.1.1 w.1.2) D

/-! ### The sunglass lemma -/

/-- The sampler of the post-processed distribution `P(X)`: draw a seed `s` of `X` and coins
`c` of `P`, output `P (X s) c`. -/
def pushSampler (P : γ → κ → δ) (X : σ → γ) : σ × κ → δ :=
  fun s => P (X s.1) s.2

/-- The sunglass reduction [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.2]: from a distinguisher `D` of
`P(X)` and `P(Y)`, the distinguisher `D ∘ P` of `X` and `Y`. On input `z` it draws coins
for `P`, runs `P` once on `z`, and calls `D` once on the result with `D`'s own coins. -/
def sunglassRed (P : γ → κ → δ) (D : δ → ρ → Bool) : γ → κ × ρ → Bool :=
  fun z c => D (P z c.1) c.2

/-- The sunglass lemma, concrete form [Gar26, Lemma 3.2]: the distinguisher `D ∘ P` has
exactly the advantage between `X` and `Y` that `D` has between `P(X)` and `P(Y)`. The
post-processing `P` may be randomized, with coins from `κ`. -/
theorem distAdv_sunglassRed (P : γ → κ → δ) (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ)
    (D : δ → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y (sunglassRed P D) = distAdv (pushSampler P X) (pushSampler P Y) D := by
  unfold distAdv sunglassRed pushSampler
  rw [acceptProb_bind, acceptProb_bind]

/-- The sunglass lemma for a deterministic post-processing map `P`: the distinguisher
`D ∘ P` has the advantage between `X` and `Y` that `D` has between `P ∘ X` and `P ∘ Y`.
[Gar26, Lemma 3.2]. -/
theorem distAdv_comp (P : γ → δ) (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (D : δ → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y (fun z r => D (P z) r) = distAdv (fun s => P (X s)) (fun s => P (Y s)) D :=
  rfl

/-! ### Mixing over an index -/

/-- The distinguisher that draws an index `k` uniformly at random and runs `D k`. In a
hybrid argument this is the uniform reduction: it does not need to know the good hybrid
index. -/
def mixDist (D : ι → γ → ρ → Bool) : γ → ι × ρ → Bool :=
  fun z c => D c.1 z c.2

/-- The acceptance probability of the mixed distinguisher is the average over `k` of the
acceptance probabilities of the `D k`. -/
theorem acceptProb_mixDist [Fintype ι] (X : σ → γ) (D : ι → γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb X (mixDist D) = uexp fun k => acceptProb X (D k) := by
  let e : σ × (ι × ρ) ≃ ι × (σ × ρ) :=
    { toFun := fun w => (w.2.1, (w.1, w.2.2)), invFun := fun v => (v.2.1, (v.1, v.2.2)),
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl, right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  unfold acceptProb mixDist
  exact (uprob_eq_of_equiv e (q := fun w : ι × (σ × ρ) => D w.1 (X w.2.1) w.2.2 = true)
    fun _ => Iff.rfl).trans (uprob_prod _)

/-- The averaged hybrid argument: if `D k` accepts `X` with probability `P k` and `Y` with
probability `P (k + 1)` for each `k < t`, then the mixed distinguisher has advantage exactly
`|P 0 - P t| / t`. [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.3], uniform version.

**Proof sketch.** The difference of the averages is the average of the differences, which
telescopes to `(P 0 - P t) / t`. -/
theorem distAdv_mixDist_eq {t : ℕ} (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (D : Fin t → γ → ρ → Bool)
    (P : ℕ → ℝ) (hX : ∀ k : Fin t, acceptProb X (D k) = P k)
    (hY : ∀ k : Fin t, acceptProb Y (D k) = P (k + 1)) :
    distAdv X Y (mixDist D) = |P 0 - P t| / t := by
  unfold distAdv
  rw [acceptProb_mixDist, acceptProb_mixDist]
  simp only [hX, hY, uexp, Fintype.card_fin]
  rw [← sub_div, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
    Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i => P i - P (i + 1)), Finset.sum_range_sub', abs_div,
    Nat.abs_cast]

/-! ### The multicopy lemma -/

/-- The `t`-product of a sampler: `t` independent copies of `X`, sampled from `t`
independent seeds. [Gar26, Lemma 3.3]. -/
def copies (t : ℕ) (X : σ → γ) : (Fin t → σ) → Fin t → γ :=
  fun s i => X (s i)

/-- The `k`-th hybrid of the multicopy lemma: the first `k` coordinates are copies of `Y`,
the remaining `t - k` copies of `X`, all independent. [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.3], the
hybrid `H_n^{(k,t)} = (Y^{(1)}, …, Y^{(k)}, X^{(k+1)}, …, X^{(t)})`. -/
def multicopyHybrid (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t k : ℕ) :
    (Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ) → Fin t → γ :=
  fun s i => if (i : ℕ) < k then Y (s.2 i) else X (s.1 i)

/-- The multicopy reduction at hybrid index `k` [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.3]: on input `z`,
sample `k` copies of `Y` and `t - k - 1` copies of `X`, place `z` at position `k`
(0-indexed), and call `D` once on the resulting tuple. It uses `t - 1` calls to the
samplers of `X` and `Y` (it draws seeds for all `t` positions and ignores two of them);
this is where efficient samplability of `X` and `Y` is used.

Deviation: [Gar26] writes `B(Z) = A(X_1, …, X_{k-1}, Z, Y_{k+1}, …, Y_t)`, with copies of
`X` before `Z` and copies of `Y` after; that does not match its own hybrids, which put the
copies of `Y` first. Here the order matches the hybrids. -/
def multicopyRed (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t k : ℕ) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    γ → ((Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) × ρ → Bool :=
  fun z c => D (fun i => if (i : ℕ) < k then Y (c.1.2 i) else if (i : ℕ) = k then z
    else X (c.1.1 i)) c.2

/-- The zeroth hybrid is the `t`-product of `X`. -/
theorem acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_zero [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t 0) D = acceptProb (copies t X) D := by
  have h : multicopyHybrid X Y t 0 = fun s => copies t X s.1 := by
    funext s i
    simp [multicopyHybrid, copies]
  rw [h, acceptProb_fst]

/-- The `t`-th hybrid is the `t`-product of `Y`. -/
theorem acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_self [Nonempty σ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t t) D = acceptProb (copies t Y) D := by
  have h : multicopyHybrid X Y t t = fun s => copies t Y s.2 := by
    funext s i
    simp [multicopyHybrid, copies]
  rw [h, acceptProb_snd]

/-- On a sample of `X`, the hybrid-`k` reduction simulates the `k`-th hybrid for `D`.

**Proof sketch.** Its input is placed at position `k`, which in the `k`-th hybrid holds a
copy of `X`; overwriting the ignored seed at position `k` with the input's seed leaves the
seed tuple uniform. -/
theorem acceptProb_multicopyRed_left [Nonempty σ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) {t k : ℕ}
    (hk : k < t) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb X (multicopyRed X Y t k D) = acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t k) D := by
  refine (acceptProb_bind X (fun z (s : (Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) (i : Fin t) =>
    if (i : ℕ) < k then Y (s.2 i) else if (i : ℕ) = k then z else X (s.1 i)) D).trans ?_
  refine Eq.trans ?_ (acceptProb_update (ρ := ρ) (⟨k, hk⟩ : Fin t)
    (fun u (s' : Fin t → τ) => multicopyHybrid X Y t k (u, s')) D)
  congr 1
  funext w i
  simp only [multicopyHybrid, Function.update_apply, Fin.ext_iff]
  rcases lt_trichotomy (i : ℕ) k with h | h | h
  · simp [h]
  · simp [h]
  · simp [h.ne', not_lt.mpr h.le]

/-- On a sample of `Y`, the hybrid-`k` reduction simulates the `(k + 1)`-th hybrid for `D`.

**Proof sketch.** As in `acceptProb_multicopyRed_left`: position `k` holds a copy of `Y` in
the `(k + 1)`-th hybrid. -/
theorem acceptProb_multicopyRed_right [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) {t k : ℕ}
    (hk : k < t) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb Y (multicopyRed X Y t k D) = acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t (k + 1)) D := by
  let e : τ × ((Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) ≃ τ × ((Fin t → τ) × (Fin t → σ)) :=
    (Equiv.refl τ).prodCongr (Equiv.prodComm _ _)
  refine (acceptProb_bind Y (fun z (s : (Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) (i : Fin t) =>
    if (i : ℕ) < k then Y (s.2 i) else if (i : ℕ) = k then z else X (s.1 i)) D).trans ?_
  refine Eq.trans ?_ ((acceptProb_comp_equiv e _ D).trans
    ((acceptProb_update (ρ := ρ) (⟨k, hk⟩ : Fin t)
      (fun u (s : Fin t → σ) => multicopyHybrid X Y t (k + 1) (s, u)) D).trans
    (acceptProb_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) (multicopyHybrid X Y t (k + 1)) D)))
  congr 1
  funext w i
  simp only [e, multicopyHybrid, Function.update_apply, Fin.ext_iff, Equiv.prodCongr_apply,
    Equiv.coe_refl, Equiv.prodComm_apply, Prod.map, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap, id]
  rcases lt_trichotomy (i : ℕ) k with h | h | h
  · simp [h, Nat.lt_succ_of_lt h, h.ne]
  · simp [h]
  · simp [h.ne', not_lt.mpr h.le, not_lt.mpr (Nat.succ_le_of_lt h)]

/-- The multicopy lemma, concrete form [Gar26, Lemma 3.3]: if `D` distinguishes `t ≥ 1`
independent copies of `X` from `t` independent copies of `Y` with advantage `ε`, then for
some hybrid index `k < t` the reduction `multicopyRed X Y t k D` distinguishes one copy with
advantage at least `ε / t`. The index `k` is the non-uniform choice of the source
(footnote 2); `distAdv_multicopyAvgRed` removes it.

**Proof sketch.** The reduction at `k` accepts `X` and `Y` with the acceptance
probabilities of hybrids `k` and `k + 1`; the end hybrids are the two `t`-products, and
some neighbouring pair of hybrids is `ε / t` apart. -/
theorem exists_multicopyRed_ge [Nonempty σ] [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) {t : ℕ}
    (ht : 0 < t) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    ∃ k < t, distAdv (copies t X) (copies t Y) D / t ≤ distAdv X Y (multicopyRed X Y t k D) := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hgap⟩ :=
    exists_hybrid_gap (fun i => acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t i) D) ht
  refine ⟨k, hk, ?_⟩
  unfold distAdv
  rw [acceptProb_multicopyRed_left X Y hk, acceptProb_multicopyRed_right X Y hk,
    ← acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_zero X Y, ← acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_self X Y]
  exact hgap

/-- The uniform multicopy reduction: draw the hybrid index `k < t` uniformly at random and
run `multicopyRed X Y t k D`. It calls `D` once and the samplers `t - 1` times. -/
def multicopyAvgRed (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t : ℕ) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    γ → Fin t × (((Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) × ρ) → Bool :=
  mixDist fun k : Fin t => multicopyRed X Y t k D

/-- The multicopy lemma with a uniform reduction: the reduction with a random hybrid index
has advantage exactly `ε / t`, where `ε` is the advantage of `D` on the `t`-products.
[Gar26, Lemma 3.3].

**Proof sketch.** Average the identities of `acceptProb_multicopyRed_left` and
`acceptProb_multicopyRed_right` over `k`; the differences telescope. -/
theorem distAdv_multicopyAvgRed [Nonempty σ] [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y (multicopyAvgRed X Y t D) = distAdv (copies t X) (copies t Y) D / t := by
  rw [multicopyAvgRed, distAdv_mixDist_eq X Y _ (fun i => acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t i) D)
    (fun k => acceptProb_multicopyRed_left X Y k.isLt D)
    (fun k => acceptProb_multicopyRed_right X Y k.isLt D), distAdv,
    acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_zero, acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_self]

end TCSlib.Cryptography
```

```text
import TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.Basic

set_option maxHeartbeats 0

set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Short integer solution: experiments and the hardness assumption

## Contents

* `Basic`: numeric parameters and the nonzero short integer kernel relation.
* `Experiments`: the concrete success probability of an optional integer-vector solver.
* `Encoding`: matrix encodings and signed outputs with proved representation guarantees.
* `Assumption`: polynomial representation budgets and success hardness against `NUPPT`.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, author version dated
  17 February 2016, Definition 4.1.1.
-/
```

## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/SIS/Assumption.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.Encoding
import TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.Experiments
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Adversary
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Negligible

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# SIS against non-uniform PPT machines

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.Family`: dimension, column count, modulus and squared-norm
  bound at each independent security parameter, with polynomial representation budgets.
* `Family.inputBitsBound`, `Family.outputBitsBound`: syntactic polynomial bounds for
  the matrix input and prescribed signed integer-vector output.
* `Family.successAt`: the concrete success probability of a binary-output machine.
* `SISAssumption`: every non-uniform PPT machine has negligible SIS success.

## Main results

* The budget and success equation lemmas and `sisAssumption_iff` expose the assumption
  without unfolding its definitions.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, author version dated
  17 February 2016, Definition 4.1.1.
* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed.,
  January 2010, Section 2.1, Definition 26.8 (non-uniform PPT adversaries).

**Representation convention.** Matrix entries use `residueBits` bits each. Solver output
uses one sign bit and `magnitudeBits` bits per integer coordinate, with malformed total
lengths rejected. The family requires
`sqNormBound < 2^magnitudeBits`, a conservative sufficient numeric condition that covers
the magnitude of every vector satisfying the norm bound. This prevents the output format
from silently excluding otherwise valid solutions. Coverage follows from the encoding
module's proved `decodeSolution_encodeSolution_of_isSolution`, rather than an additional
correctness hypothesis in this family.

These are mathematical finite-distribution experiments. Efficient parameter generation,
matrix sampling and implementation of encoders/decoders remain separate construction
obligations. In particular an exact fair-bit matrix sampler needs a power-of-two modulus
or a separate sampling argument. The bundle does not assert that solutions exist or that
the norm bound excludes trivial multiples of the modulus. Parameter profiles must check
those facts separately. SIS hardness is independent of LWE throughout this module.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS

open Complexity

/-- An asymptotic SIS family with a separate security parameter
[Pei16, Definition 4.1.1; PS10, Definition 26.8]. Dimensions and representation widths
have syntactic polynomial bounds. The numeric squared-norm bound must fit the output
magnitude width so that short solutions are representable.

**Convention.** This bundle asserts representation bounds, not uniform computability or
efficiency of an honest sampler. Those contracts are separate from hardness. -/
structure Family where
  /-- Numeric dimension, column count, modulus and squared-norm bound. -/
  parameters : ℕ → Parameters
  /-- A syntactic polynomial upper bound on the public matrix's row count. -/
  dimensionBound : PolyExpr
  /-- A syntactic polynomial upper bound on the public matrix's column count. -/
  columnsBound : PolyExpr
  /-- The fixed-width binary representation of each matrix entry. -/
  residueBits : PolyExpr
  /-- The unsigned magnitude width in each signed output coordinate. -/
  magnitudeBits : PolyExpr
  /-- The matrix dimension is polynomially bounded. -/
  dimension_le : ∀ κ, (parameters κ).dimension ≤ dimensionBound.eval κ
  /-- The number of output coordinates is polynomially bounded. -/
  columns_le : ∀ κ, (parameters κ).columns ≤ columnsBound.eval κ
  /-- Every matrix residue fits without truncation. -/
  modulus_le_pow : ∀ κ, (parameters κ).modulus ≤ 2 ^ (residueBits.eval κ)
  /-- Conservative coverage condition: the entire squared-norm bound fits in the
  magnitude width, hence so does every coordinate of a valid solution. -/
  sqNormBound_lt_pow : ∀ κ, (parameters κ).sqNormBound < 2 ^ (magnitudeBits.eval κ)

namespace Family

/-- The syntactic polynomial `dimensionBound * columnsBound * residueBits` bounds
the public SIS matrix encoding [Pei16, Definition 4.1.1, representation accounting]. -/
def inputBitsBound (F : Family) : PolyExpr :=
  .mul (.mul F.dimensionBound F.columnsBound) F.residueBits

/-- `F.inputBitsBound` is the expression
`dimensionBound * columnsBound * residueBits`. -/
theorem inputBitsBound_eq (F : Family) :
    F.inputBitsBound = .mul (.mul F.dimensionBound F.columnsBound) F.residueBits := rfl

/-- The syntactic polynomial `columnsBound * (magnitudeBits + 1)` bounds the prescribed
signed integer-vector output [Pei16, Definition 4.1.1, representation accounting]. -/
def outputBitsBound (F : Family) : PolyExpr :=
  .mul F.columnsBound (.add F.magnitudeBits (.const 1))

/-- `F.outputBitsBound` is the expression `columnsBound * (magnitudeBits + 1)`. -/
theorem outputBitsBound_eq (F : Family) :
    F.outputBitsBound = .mul F.columnsBound (.add F.magnitudeBits (.const 1)) := rfl

/-- Every SIS challenge fits the family's syntactic polynomial input budget.

**Proof sketch.** Substitute `encodeChallenge_length`, apply the numeric dimension and
column bounds, and read `PolyExpr`'s addition/multiplication equations. -/
theorem encodeChallenge_length_le (F : Family) (κ : ℕ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin (F.parameters κ).dimension) (Fin (F.parameters κ).columns)
      (ZMod (F.parameters κ).modulus)) :
    (encodeChallenge (F.parameters κ) (F.residueBits.eval κ) A).length ≤
      F.inputBitsBound.eval κ := by
  rw [encodeChallenge_length, inputBitsBound_eq, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_mul]
  exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.mul_le_mul (F.dimension_le κ) (F.columns_le κ))

/-- The signed encoding of every candidate fits the prescribed polynomial output budget.

**Proof sketch.** Substitute `encodeSolution_length` and apply `columns_le`, with the
common nonnegative coordinate width `magnitudeBits + 1`. -/
theorem encodeSolution_length_le (F : Family) (κ : ℕ)
    (z : Fin (F.parameters κ).columns → ℤ) :
    (encodeSolution (F.parameters κ) (F.magnitudeBits.eval κ) z).length ≤
      F.outputBitsBound.eval κ := by
  rw [encodeSolution_length, outputBitsBound_eq, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_add,
    PolyExpr.eval_const]
  exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (F.columns_le κ)

/-- The SIS success probability of an `NUPPT` at parameter `κ`
[Pei16, Definition 4.1.1; PS10, Definition 26.8]. The machine receives the canonical
public-matrix encoding, and its output is decoded as an exact-length signed integer
vector. A malformed output fails; a decoded output must still satisfy the full integer
solution relation tested by `successProbability`. -/
noncomputable def successAt (F : Family) (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  successProbability (F.parameters κ)
    (fun A r => decodeSolution (F.parameters κ) (F.magnitudeBits.eval κ)
      (D.runAt κ (encodeChallenge (F.parameters κ) (F.residueBits.eval κ) A) r))

/-- `F.successAt D κ` is the concrete SIS success probability with the machine run
on encoded matrices and its output passed through `decodeSolution`. -/
theorem successAt_eq (F : Family) (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) :
    F.successAt D κ = successProbability (F.parameters κ)
      (fun A r => decodeSolution (F.parameters κ) (F.magnitudeBits.eval κ)
        (D.runAt κ (encodeChallenge (F.parameters κ) (F.residueBits.eval κ) A) r)) := rfl

end Family

/-- The SIS assumption for this parameter family: every non-uniform PPT machine has
negligible success at producing a nonzero short integer kernel vector
[Pei16, Definition 4.1.1; PS10, Definition 26.8]. This is a proposition supplied by
consumers, not a theorem, axiom or consequence of the LWE assumption. -/
def SISAssumption (F : Family) : Prop :=
  ∀ D : NUPPT, Negligible fun κ => F.successAt D κ

/-- `SISAssumption F` holds exactly when `F.successAt D` is negligible for every
non-uniform PPT machine `D`. -/
theorem sisAssumption_iff (F : Family) :
    SISAssumption F ↔ ∀ D : NUPPT, Negligible fun κ => F.successAt D κ := Iff.rfl

end TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS
```


## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/SIS/Basic.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Mul
import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# SIS parameters and the short integer kernel relation

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.Parameters`: dimensions, modulus, and squared Euclidean bound.
* `IsSolution`: a nonzero short integer vector annihilated by the matrix modulo its modulus.

## Main results

* `isSolution_iff` exposes the nonzero, squared-norm and kernel conditions.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, author version dated
  17 February 2016, Definition 4.1.1.

**Deviation.** The bound is an integer bound on the squared Euclidean norm, explicitly
named `sqNormBound`, instead of a real bound on the Euclidean norm. Matrices have `n`
rows and `m` columns. No assumption about existence of short solutions, hardness, or a
connection with LWE is part of the numeric bundle or the solution relation.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS

/-- Numeric SIS parameters: a matrix with `dimension` rows and `columns` columns modulo
`modulus >= 2`, and an integer upper bound on squared Euclidean solution norm
[Pei16, Definition 4.1.1, squared-bound formulation]. -/
structure Parameters where
  /-- The number of rows of the public matrix. -/
  dimension : ℕ
  /-- The number of columns, hence coordinates of a solution. -/
  columns : ℕ
  /-- The modulus of the kernel equation. -/
  modulus : ℕ
  /-- The allowed upper bound on `sum_i z_i^2`. -/
  sqNormBound : ℕ
  /-- The modulus is at least two. -/
  modulus_ge_two : 2 ≤ modulus

instance (P : Parameters) : NeZero P.modulus :=
  ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.zero_lt_succ 1) P.modulus_ge_two)⟩

/-- An SIS solution is an integer vector that is nonzero over the integers, has squared
Euclidean norm at most `sqNormBound`, and maps to zero under the matrix modulo the
modulus [Pei16, Definition 4.1.1, squared-bound formulation]. Nonzeroness is deliberately
not tested after reduction modulo the modulus. -/
def IsSolution (P : Parameters)
    (A : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus))
    (z : Fin P.columns → ℤ) : Prop :=
  z ≠ 0 ∧ (∑ i, z i ^ 2) ≤ (P.sqNormBound : ℤ) ∧
    A.mulVec (fun i => (z i : ZMod P.modulus)) = 0

/-- The SIS relation holds exactly when the integer vector is nonzero, its sum of
squared coordinates is bounded, and its reduction lies in the matrix's modular kernel. -/
theorem isSolution_iff (P : Parameters)
    (A : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus))
    (z : Fin P.columns → ℤ) :
    IsSolution P A z ↔ z ≠ 0 ∧ (∑ i, z i ^ 2) ≤ (P.sqNormBound : ℤ) ∧
      A.mulVec (fun i => (z i : ZMod P.modulus)) = 0 := Iff.rfl

end TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS
```

```text
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.Modular
import TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.List.Lemmas

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary SIS inputs and fixed-width signed solver outputs

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.encodeChallenge`: the row-major public matrix.
* `decodeSolution`: decode an exact-length sign-and-magnitude integer vector, rejecting
  every output whose total length differs from the prescribed length.
* `encodeSolution`: concatenate one sign-and-magnitude block for each integer coordinate.

## Main results

* `encodeChallenge_eq`, `decodeSolution_eq` expose the input encoding and output parser.
* `decodeSolution_of_length_ne`: a malformed output length is rejected.
* The length, input injectivity and signed round-trip theorems establish faithful
  representation, including coverage of every solution under the prescribed norm bound.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, author version dated
  17 February 2016, Definition 4.1.1.
* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed.,
  January 2010, Section 2.1 (binary-string machine inputs and outputs).

**Representation convention.** Input entries are fixed-width nonnegative representatives
of residues, in row-major order. Output coordinate `i` occupies one sign bit followed by
`magnitudeBits` magnitude bits, most significant bit first. Sign `true` means negative.
The output length must be exactly `P.columns * (magnitudeBits + 1)`. Negative zero is
accepted and decodes to zero, so the signed output representation is deliberately not
unique. This causes no ambiguity in the integer solution relation.

The parser is total, and malformed lengths return `none`. It does not itself test the
norm, nonzeroness or kernel equation: the concrete SIS success experiment tests all of
them. The asymptotic family requires a magnitude width sufficient for every valid bounded
solution. Decoder completeness, lengths and input faithfulness are proved below,
rather than stored as additional correctness hypotheses in the hardness assumption.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS

/-- Encode the public SIS matrix [Pei16, Definition 4.1.1] in row-major order, using
the common modular representation. It retains every residue when
`P.modulus <= 2^width`. -/
def encodeChallenge (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus)) : List Bool :=
  Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix width A

/-- `encodeChallenge P width A` is the common row-major `encodeMatrix width A`. -/
theorem encodeChallenge_eq (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus)) :
    encodeChallenge P width A = Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix width A := rfl

/-- Decode a binary machine output as the integer vector required by SIS
[Pei16, Definition 4.1.1; PS10, Section 2.1]. Each coordinate is a sign bit (`true`
means negative) followed by a fixed-width nonnegative magnitude. Reject a wrong total
length. Both signs of zero decode to the same integer zero; the decoder does not claim
that the signed representation is unique. -/
def decodeSolution (P : Parameters) (magnitudeBits : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    Option (Fin P.columns → ℤ) :=
  if w.length = P.columns * (magnitudeBits + 1) then
    some (fun i =>
      let magnitude := NumberTheory.listToNat
        ((w.drop (i.val * (magnitudeBits + 1) + 1)).take magnitudeBits)
      if w.getD (i.val * (magnitudeBits + 1)) false then
        -(magnitude : ℤ)
      else
        (magnitude : ℤ))
  else none

/-- `decodeSolution P magnitudeBits w` is `none` for a wrong total length; otherwise
coordinate `i` is the signed magnitude in its block of `magnitudeBits + 1` bits. -/
theorem decodeSolution_eq (P : Parameters) (magnitudeBits : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    decodeSolution P magnitudeBits w =
      if w.length = P.columns * (magnitudeBits + 1) then
        some (fun i =>
          let magnitude := NumberTheory.listToNat
            ((w.drop (i.val * (magnitudeBits + 1) + 1)).take magnitudeBits)
          if w.getD (i.val * (magnitudeBits + 1)) false then
            -(magnitude : ℤ)
          else
            (magnitude : ℤ))
      else none := rfl

/-- If `w.length` is not `P.columns * (magnitudeBits + 1)`, then
`decodeSolution P magnitudeBits w = none`. -/
theorem decodeSolution_of_length_ne (P : Parameters) (magnitudeBits : ℕ) (w : List Bool)
    (h : w.length ≠ P.columns * (magnitudeBits + 1)) :
    decodeSolution P magnitudeBits w = none := by
  rw [decodeSolution_eq, if_neg h]

/-- Encode an integer solution candidate as one sign bit and a fixed-width magnitude
per coordinate. Sign `true` means negative, and zero is written with sign `false`.
Magnitudes are lossless when each is less than `2^magnitudeBits`; the underlying numeral
operation is total and truncates larger magnitudes. This is representation plumbing for
the integer vectors in [Pei16, Definition 4.1.1]. -/
def encodeSolution (P : Parameters) (magnitudeBits : ℕ) (z : Fin P.columns → ℤ) :
    List Bool :=
  (List.ofFn fun i => decide (z i < 0) ::
    Candidates.natToList magnitudeBits (z i).natAbs).flatten

/-- `encodeSolution` concatenates the negative-sign test followed by the fixed-width
absolute-value numeral for each coordinate in increasing order. -/
theorem encodeSolution_eq (P : Parameters) (magnitudeBits : ℕ) (z : Fin P.columns → ℤ) :
    encodeSolution P magnitudeBits z =
      (List.ofFn fun i => decide (z i < 0) ::
        Candidates.natToList magnitudeBits (z i).natAbs).flatten := rfl

/-- An encoded SIS matrix has exactly `dimension * columns * width` bits.

**Proof sketch.** Read `encodeChallenge_eq` and apply the common matrix-length statement. -/
theorem encodeChallenge_length (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus)) :
    (encodeChallenge P width A).length = P.dimension * P.columns * width := by
  rw [encodeChallenge_eq, Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix_length]

/-- The SIS matrix encoding is injective when every modular entry fits in the width.

**Proof sketch.** Read `encodeChallenge_eq` and use the common matrix injectivity statement. -/
theorem encodeChallenge_injective (P : Parameters) (width : ℕ)
    (hwidth : P.modulus ≤ 2 ^ width) :
    Function.Injective (encodeChallenge P width) := by
  intro A B h
  apply Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix_injective width hwidth
  simpa only [encodeChallenge_eq] using h

/-- The signed encoding has exactly one sign bit and `magnitudeBits` magnitude bits
per integer coordinate, including when there are no coordinates or zero magnitude bits.

**Proof sketch.** Every block is a singleton sign followed by a numeral of the prescribed
length; add those equal block lengths over all coordinates. -/
theorem encodeSolution_length (P : Parameters) (magnitudeBits : ℕ) (z : Fin P.columns → ℤ) :
    (encodeSolution P magnitudeBits z).length = P.columns * (magnitudeBits + 1) := by
  rw [encodeSolution_eq, List.length_flatten, ← List.ofFn_comp']
  simp only [List.length_cons, Candidates.length_natToList, List.ofFn_const,
    List.sum_replicate_nat]

/-- Decoding a signed encoding recovers every coordinate whose magnitude fits.

**Proof sketch.** The length statement opens the decoder's successful branch. The
fixed-offset block slices recover each sign and numeral, the existing numeral round trip
recovers its magnitude, and the integer sign/absolute-value identities recover the integer.
The zero-coordinate and zero-magnitude-width cases are included. -/
theorem decodeSolution_encodeSolution (P : Parameters) (magnitudeBits : ℕ)
    (z : Fin P.columns → ℤ) (hfit : ∀ i, (z i).natAbs < 2 ^ magnitudeBits) :
    decodeSolution P magnitudeBits (encodeSolution P magnitudeBits z) = some z := by
  let blocks : Fin P.columns → List Bool := fun i =>
    decide (z i < 0) :: Candidates.natToList magnitudeBits (z i).natAbs
  have hencoded :
      encodeSolution P magnitudeBits z = (List.ofFn blocks).flatten :=
    encodeSolution_eq P magnitudeBits z
  have hblockLength (j : Fin P.columns) :
      (blocks j).length = magnitudeBits + 1 := by
    change
      (decide (z j < 0) ::
        Candidates.natToList magnitudeBits (z j).natAbs).length =
          magnitudeBits + 1
    rw [List.length_cons, Candidates.length_natToList]
  have hmap :
      (List.ofFn blocks).map List.length =
        List.replicate P.columns (magnitudeBits + 1) := by
    calc
      _ = List.ofFn (fun j => (blocks j).length) :=
        List.map_ofFn blocks List.length
      _ = List.ofFn (fun _ : Fin P.columns => magnitudeBits + 1) :=
        congrArg List.ofFn (funext hblockLength)
      _ = _ := List.ofFn_const P.columns (magnitudeBits + 1)
  have hprefix (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ P.columns) :
      (((List.ofFn blocks).map List.length).take j).sum =
        j * (magnitudeBits + 1) := by
    rw [hmap, List.take_replicate, Nat.min_eq_left hj, List.sum_replicate_nat]
  rw [decodeSolution_eq, encodeSolution_length, if_pos rfl]
  apply congrArg some
  funext i
  have hblock :
      ((List.ofFn blocks).flatten.drop
        (i.val * (magnitudeBits + 1))).take (magnitudeBits + 1) =
          blocks i := by
    have h := List.drop_take_succ_flatten_eq_getElem
      (List.ofFn blocks) i.val
      (by simpa only [List.length_ofFn] using i.isLt)
    rw [hprefix (i.val + 1) (Nat.succ_le_of_lt i.isLt),
      hprefix i.val (Nat.le_of_lt i.isLt),
      List.drop_take, Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul,
      Nat.add_sub_cancel_left] at h
    simpa only [List.getElem_ofFn] using h
  have hsign :
      (List.ofFn blocks).flatten.getD
        (i.val * (magnitudeBits + 1)) false =
          decide (z i < 0) := by
    have h := congrArg (fun xs : List Bool => xs.getD 0 false) hblock
    simpa only [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD,
      List.getElem?_take_of_lt (Nat.zero_lt_succ magnitudeBits),
      List.getElem?_drop, Nat.add_zero, blocks,
      List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.getD_some] using h
  have hmagnitude :
      ((List.ofFn blocks).flatten.drop
        (i.val * (magnitudeBits + 1) + 1)).take magnitudeBits =
          Candidates.natToList magnitudeBits (z i).natAbs := by
    have h := congrArg (fun xs : List Bool => xs.drop 1) hblock
    simpa only [List.drop_take, List.drop_drop, Nat.add_sub_cancel,
      blocks, List.drop_succ_cons, List.drop_zero] using h
  rw [hencoded, hsign, hmagnitude, Candidates.listToNat_natToList (hfit i)]
  change
    (if decide (z i < 0) then -((z i).natAbs : ℤ)
      else ((z i).natAbs : ℤ)) = z i
  by_cases hneg : z i < 0
  · rw [if_pos (decide_eq_true hneg),
      Int.ofNat_natAbs_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hneg), Int.neg_neg]
  · have hd : decide (z i < 0) ≠ true := by
      intro h
      exact hneg (of_decide_eq_true h)
    rw [if_neg hd]
    exact Int.natAbs_of_nonneg (le_of_not_gt hneg)

/-- Every valid SIS solution is representable in the prescribed signed format when
the squared-norm bound is less than `2^magnitudeBits` [Pei16, Definition 4.1.1,
squared-bound representation].

**Proof sketch.** A coordinate square is at most the total sum of squares, so a solution's
integer absolute coordinate is at most the natural squared-norm bound. The given strict
inequality makes each magnitude fit; apply `decodeSolution_encodeSolution`. -/
theorem decodeSolution_encodeSolution_of_isSolution (P : Parameters) (magnitudeBits : ℕ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus))
    (z : Fin P.columns → ℤ) (hsolution : IsSolution P A z)
    (hfit : P.sqNormBound < 2 ^ magnitudeBits) :
    decodeSolution P magnitudeBits (encodeSolution P magnitudeBits z) = some z := by
  apply decodeSolution_encodeSolution P magnitudeBits z
  intro i
  have hnorm := ((isSolution_iff P A z).mp hsolution).2.1
  have hcoordinate : z i ^ 2 ≤ ∑ j, z j ^ 2 :=
    Finset.single_le_sum (fun j _ => sq_nonneg (z j)) (Finset.mem_univ i)
  have hbound : ((z i).natAbs : ℤ) ≤ (P.sqNormBound : ℤ) :=
    (Int.natAbs_le_self_sq (z i)).trans (hcoordinate.trans hnorm)
  exact lt_of_le_of_lt (Int.ofNat_le.mp hbound) hfit

end TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS
```

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.Basic
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Probability
import Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Basic

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The concrete SIS success experiment

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS.successProbability`: the probability that an adversary
  outputs a valid short, nonzero integer solution for an independent uniform matrix.

## Main results

* `successProbability_eq` exposes the experiment as a uniform probability.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, author version dated
  17 February 2016, Definition 4.1.1.

The solver can fail by returning `none`. It otherwise returns an integer vector, not a
vector of residues; validity includes the full integer norm bound and nonzeroness.
There is no restriction on running time in this concrete experiment. No LWE assumption
or lattice reduction is used.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS

variable {ρ : Type*} [Fintype ρ]

/-- The SIS success probability samples a uniform public matrix and independent uniform
solver coins, then checks the solver's optional integer vector against `IsSolution`
[Pei16, Definition 4.1.1, squared-bound formulation]. A `none` answer is unsuccessful. -/
noncomputable def successProbability [Nonempty ρ] (P : Parameters)
    (solve : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus) →
      ρ → Option (Fin P.columns → ℤ)) : ℝ :=
  uprob fun r : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus) × ρ =>
    match solve r.1 r.2 with
    | none => False
    | some z => IsSolution P r.1 z

/-- SIS success is the uniform probability that the optional answer is present and
satisfies the integer solution relation for the sampled matrix. -/
theorem successProbability_eq [Nonempty ρ] (P : Parameters)
    (solve : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus) →
      ρ → Option (Fin P.columns → ℤ)) :
    successProbability P solve =
      uprob fun r : Matrix (Fin P.dimension) (Fin P.columns) (ZMod P.modulus) × ρ =>
        match solve r.1 r.2 with
        | none => False
        | some z => IsSolution P r.1 z := rfl

end TCSlib.Cryptography.SIS
```
